construction_sents: The extra step of cleaning with vinegar to get the oils out is just too time consuming with an active one.
/>What I love about this product is it's hard plastic and made in the USA, so I trust the standards and manufacturing process a bit more.
The tray has a nice side cup holder/section for foods you want to keep separated from the larger compartment.
Good size for the portion she usually eats.

In terms of not having bottom suction like silicone plates do, that didn't matter to us since my daughter always managed to lift her plates anyway.

The bowl is really what attracted me to the set.
We only had silicone plates, so were using small Corelle and vitrified condiment bowls to serve her anything that was soupy.
Not great when you're in the toddler independent  phase.
The bowl is light enough for her to tilt and scoop from but not too deep that she has a hard time seeing into it.
Fork isn't as usable for her as the ends are, naturally, blunted for her child safety.
She was able to spear a small piece of garlic bread and chomp from it
so I think she likes it.
/>As to the cup, I wish there were a straw lid option as my 1.5yo never learned to drink from a sippy cup.
The lid material is silicone and the cup itself the same material as the rest of the pieces.

We'll maybe let her use it as an open cup once she's gotten the hang of drinking from a tiny open cup first.

Lastly, the set is SO much easier to clean than silicone.
No oil sticking or absorbing or weird smells.
Foods rinses off easily.
Probably no need to mention that we're happy with this product, but there you go.
We have a couple different brands of smocks for our 1yo and these are on the higher end quality of design and material.
The plastic has a texture to it that makes it feel more like a fabric.
Another set we tried was a smooth plastic that wore down really quickly with staining and a melted feel after a few months of hand washing and air drying.
These are so much better!

Though they're easy to wipe clean immediately after use, love that they can be machine washed-- we also have pouches of the same material from this brand and they've also come out of the wash perfectly.
In terms of use, we love these smocks for messier-free meals and carry one of them in our diaper bag as back up.
I would personally prefer string ties for the neck as our 1yo is on the smaller side and have found ties work best, but the velcro is quick and doesn't pull on her hair.
The pocket is standard and we find that it doesn't really catch food in the high chair so we place a silicone bib over the smock.
Very pleased with these.
I have this set in 12-18mo and wanted these in the larger size for additional sleepwear and for my daughter to wear as she grows.
They're high quality, soft cotton with nice double zip and top tab.
They will be getting a lot of wear hopefully for a few more years since she is on the smaller side.
I have this set in addition to another pattern and like that these are gender neutral (because girls can like dinos too).
The material is high quality, love that they are made out of recycled plastic, and construction is good.
We plan to use these in our diaper bag for storing feeding and first aid supplies.
I'm not sure how fresh things like crackers would stay and definitely not sure how leak proof they would be for wet snacks so we're happy to just use them for organizing.
TBH I didn't read the specs before ordering these but I had originally wanted to use the largest size to store my daughter's silicone bib in the diaper backpack.
Not large enough unless I fold the bib into fourths.
The construction is high quality with the seams on the interior cleanly sewn and without any loose threads.
There are also cleaning instructions on the interior care tag.
Love that they can be machine washed.
Though you can supposedly use these for fruit, I'd probably reserve our Stashers for that instead as I'm not sure how leak proof these are.
Will be great for food pouches, utensils, and small baby essentials.

The pattern is cute and I do actually like that it also includes two solid rose colored pouches so that the set is not pattern overloaded and if you are using the same size in the same bag/luggage, you can tell the difference in contents easily with the patterned vs solid.
We personally won't be using these for loose snacks but will find other great uses for them.
My 1.5yo is smaller for her age but I got the 2-3T for her to grow into and wear without her feet slipping through the openings for the time being.
The TOG 2.5 sack is a good weight and thickness that she can wear during the winter, spring, and fall as we keep the temperature in the nursery regulated with a Dyson year round.
The construction has been well thought.
Seams are clean, nice 2-way zip with tabs on each end to hide the zippers, plastic snap buttons for easy diaper changes (and can be left snapped closed otherwise), and the pattern is adorable.
Will update once it's gone through the wash.
This baby wash is a new favorite!
The scent is subtle but my daughter's hair retains the scent through the next day, even through sweaty crying.
It's gentle on her skin and eyes and foams nicely off the pump.
It builds even more foam in the hair when lathering.
With the other baby wash brand we've used, rinsing still leaves the skin soapy-feeling (although maybe that's the moisturizing part of the soap?)
but the Dove rinses off cleanly and doesn't leave any doubt that there's still soap on my daughter's skin.
I like the narrow width of this edge protector.
Discreet, yet enough protection for the corner.
I did find the adhesive to be not as strong as some other ones I've used.
Noticeably more air bubbles than other protectors  I have used.
These sleep sacks are quite larger than I expected the 12-18mo size to be but that actually works perfectly for my 18mo, who is on the smaller side for her age, to continue to grow into.
The cotton is soft and feels high quality.
The top fabric tab to hide the zipper and the 2-way zip are nice touches.
These will get much use.
They come in a bundle wrapped in ribbon and packaged in a plastic bag so would make for a nice gift as well.
These are a nice lightweight but still substantial-feeling cotton sleep sacks.
but she'll still have plenty of time to continue to grow into these.
I consider the patterns to be gender neutral altho they're traditionally boy patterns.
I got these because my daughter is into the moon and stars and knows what rockets are.
The only thing I don't like about the graphic patterns is that it has aliens-- kind of ruins what could have been a really nice design.
High quality, pattern not withstanding.
Not the most attractive looking device, but it certainly does its job well.
You push in each arm and twist to unlock it which enables you to fold the arms.
It does hold well against the door handle, just not very discreet looking.
This set of fabric bow clips comes with a nice range of colors.
I have another set that is more vintage and muted neutral tones that don't work with all of my daughter's outfits.
This set includes some brighter (but not too bright) shades too.
The packaging says they are handmade.
The knot at the center of the bow is not glued or sewn, so the bow will come apart if pulled on.
My daughter has a tendency to pull on things so we'll see if these remain intact.

In regards to the clip, it is a flimsier metal piece covered with a strip of grosgrain ribbon, and then a small clear strip to provide some traction on the inside of the clip and is attached with adhesive.
The first bow I took out, the clear strip was not aligned to the clip, so I removed it to straighten out.
This made the entire clip bend 30°, tho the metal is soft enough to bend back straight easily.
The strip of grosgrain doesn't cover the metal spring
so I'll have to see if my daughter's hair gets stuck in it.
Aesthetically, the bows are pretty.
Functionally, will have to see.
This is a pretty basic headband and bow clip organizer, more functional than decorative.
The straps are sturdy and there's plenty of space and hooks for headbands.
My daughter has a ton of bow clips, though, so I was only able to clip 8 large pairs and 5 small pairs.
It would have worked better for my use of there were 2 rows for bows (6 total vertical strips) and 2 rows for headbands.
I do like that it comes with plastic S-hooks; another organizer I tried out had metal claw clips that I was afraid would damage the headband fabric.
This headband organizer doubled beautifully as wall decor.
The quality of the rope pattern, dowel rods, and wooden rings are great.
I'm not sure that I would use this organizer for bow clips since it seems awkward to clip each pair together.
I actually ended up removing all of the clips because the teeth are somewhat sharp
and I'm afraid they would ruin any fabric that is accidentally pulled on.
My husband even pinched himself handling them.
Instead, I hung small plastic S-hooks on the wooden rings.
This will hopefully make it easier to grab my daughter's headbands without worrying about damaging them.
A nice addition would have been if there were a section of vertical strips to attach bow clips to like some other similar hair accessory organizers.
Headphones come with a nice storage bag and 2 straps, pink and blue.
Straps are soft and elastic.

I've tested the muffs on my ears and they're pretty comfortable and the noise-cancelling is noticeable.

I can't compare to the headphone style vs this head strap style but my 1.5yo LO was not having it.
I had a hard time adjusting the tightness of strap while my child was squirming.
I'm hoping it would be easier when they get older!
The tub is a good size and depth for our growing toddler.
It is foldable and collapsible which is a plus for small bathroom storage solution.
It comes with a soft infant insert which we did not use.
For us the, good ends there.
/>The temperature sensor is only in Celsius and stopped working after one use.
By the end of the bath, the display had stopped working.

Upon opening the battery cover, it was wet and easy to see there is zero waterproofing to it.

The plastic feels cheap, but probably not to the point where it'll break or anything.
Update: These were a hit!
They do have a strong scent of the spices but the taste is more subtle.
The serving size is pretty generous.

We've had leftover when we use the pouch to top off dine-out meals but when served as a snack, it's been completely consumed.

-----
/>[Haven't let my daughter try this yet so will update once she does.]
The Serenity Kids puffs are my daughter's favorite
so I jumped at ordering these when I saw them.
Love that there are only 9 ingredients, all familiar and mostly organic.
Each pouch is a good snack size with a high quality twist top to make for easy saving/refrigerating if it isn't finished in one sitting.
Minimal packaging that can all be recycled (pouches via terracycle).
The box has a perforated opening all around to easily remove the top and allow for display storage in the pantry.
These are thoughtful details that I appreciate on top of the healthy smoothie ingredients!
We like that the lock is hidden inside the door.
The magnet mechanism is great and works seamlessly.
I do find that sometimes I pull on the door forgetting it's locked because it is hidden haha.

You can keep the lock in a "stay open" position so you can use the door normally, which is a great feature to have.

Installation is pretty easy after the first time.
The bracket guide that comes with it makes it simple.
I did find that the bracket doesn't really hold the two pieces in place so that was a little annoying because they keep falling out.
/>We also use the bonus rope lock on a cabinet that's more frequently used and further away from the magnet key.
It has a simple adjustable clip and is much faster to use.
As you can see it works perfectly with the type of door handle on it.
Pretty much the same type of gates as everything out there.
Pressure mounted, safety button and lift to open the gate.
We've installed a few baby gates over the years and found that this gate was sturdy and definitely had the most detailed installation instructions.
I liked how wide these strips are and worked great to protect my car in the garage.
The adhesive is good and has held up well so far!
/>I personally think because of the width it's too visible to use on furniture or wall.
But for my use, the wider width is perfect.
First, I really like that this nail clipper includes a cap.
Because my husband and I are not great at keeping up with trimming our 1yo's nails, they tend to grow a bit long.

We have an electric trimmer but I wanted to give a manual clipper a try as a lighter and smaller option to pack on trips as well as for quicker/instant clipping as opposed to the more time consuming effort of sanding her nails short.
While the clipper is easy and comfortable to handle, our daughter was not having it when I tried to trim her toe nails.
Likely due to her already being used to the electric trimmer and feeling some weird metal object under her long nails.
She's also aware enough to say no and try to kick away, so perhaps this will work on a less mobile child or introduced as an infant to they are used to it by toddlerhood.
My first attempt at using it was met with failure but I would probably still pack this with my baby travel gear essentials.
Instructions were easy to follow and very easy to install.
It has a pretty slim profile and the mechanism to lock and unlock is easy and intuitive.
far it has a pretty secure hold on the drawer and is easily adjustable if needed.
We are past the swaddle stage but like to use these to cover the stroller and car seat when our daughter is napping.
She likes bunnies, so it will give her something to look at when the rest of her view is obstructed.
High quality material, the pink isn't overly bright, and actually feels a tiny bit thicker in comparison to our popular a+a muslin blankets.
Love that it's organic and so soft.
The drawstring pouch that it comes with is identical in material I believe and will make it handy for packing for away trips.
We like the no drill option for this retractable baby gate.
Installation instructions were clear and easy to follow.

So far the no drill option has held up pretty well.

The retracting mechanism is pretty easy to use.
It can get loud when it retracts if you don't push the button down
/>As other reviews have mentioned, the price is definitely overpriced at this point for what you are getting.
Ordered this because my 1yo kept grabbing the Roku remote.
We opted for the blue one for a little more fun than the black and also the dino strap.
In the stock photos, it was difficult to tell that the images of the back were in fact images of the back; wasn't sure if it was like a thinner silicone case to put on the main remote.
So I'm not actually sure what the purpose of the back design is since it's just shapes and, as another reviewer mentioned, can be difficult to clean given the depth and tiny size of those shapes.
Nevertheless, this has been a toddler-friendly substitute for the real thing, thankfully.
We already owned an insulated FreeSip and were familiar with this brand.
Our 1yo started drinking from ours at 9mo
so we wanted her to have her own to avoid getting food all over our spout.
/>My favorite feature of the FreeSip is that you don't need to tilt the bottle to drink.
The spout is covered by a cap, so if it rolls in dirt, we won't need to worry about sanitizing or stuff getting down the straw.
The spout to another popular brand that our daughter got as a bday gift was completely exposed, which we didn't love.

This spout is also soft silicone, so she can gnaw on it as much as she wants.

With
the removable straw, the Owala is pretty easy to clean.
A straw brush fits through both the straw and spout.
The call and straw are dishwasher safe but we have had to try that yet as we hand wash frequently.
/>We haven't taken advantage of the insulated feature yet since we're in the middle of New England winter.
But I can anticipate come summertime that adding ice when we go out will make a huge difference.
/>The only learning curve for younger kids is the cap.
Instead of lifting and opening or pressing a button to pop the cap open, you have to press down in the handle towards the back.
The trickiest part for my daughter is in closing the cap (and even I forget sometimes).
You need to lift the handle at the back to snap close, which is less intuitive for toddlers IMO.
My daughter frequently pushes down on the spout because it's right in front of her view and then her fingers get stuck or the cap pops back open.
We're still trying to teach her how to close it properly.
But overall, we've loved this brand.
We have used all types of nasal aspirator - the nosefrida, electric aspirator and then this one.
The nosefrida was good for a little bit then it got annoying when the mouthpiece keeps falling out and having to clean and replace the filter.
Then we got an electric aspirator that works well but it's louder and sometimes scared our LO.
This is our latest aspirator to test out.
So far I liked the pump because it can be used easily with one hand.
It is quiet like the nosefrida but without the parts falling out on me.
It's not loud like the electric aspirator so wasn't as intimidating.
It can generate pretty good suction power depending on how fast you pull on the pump.
I think we'll use a combination of this + the electric aspirator going forward.
/>My only complaint is that it doesn't give direction on what the 2 silicone attachments are for.
It fits into the suction piece and has smaller hole, so I assume it's to use with smaller nostrils or younger kids.
This faucet extender has a very cute design and has great extension.
I like that it has two ways of using it, top down or out the back

so it's good for different types of faucets.

We are able to use the top down method on our faucet
and it feels more secure.
Because our faucet is not straight down but has a slight angle, sometimes water does get trapped in the "mouth" but that's due to our type of faucet.
Though not a bad thing as it is clearly advertised, the width of this strip is very wide at almost an inch on each side when folded over the edge.
It would be very noticeable on furniture or wall corners.
heldout_sents: I got the largest size so my 1.5yo can continue to wear it as she grows.
The double zip is great for diaper changing-- unlike most other sleep sacks, this one zips around the bottom of the sack instead of straight down the center.
Only thing I could do without is the large branding on the top.
Because the colors are pastel, the logo patch stands out so much.
Found it unnecessary since there's also a tag that sticks out the the bottom with the care tags.

We started our 1.5yo on silicone feeding supplies like a straw cup and plates but wasn't a fan of how any liquid or food would absorb the silicone flavor nor that the silicone would absorb the food odors.
I don't think she knows the difference,but my husband and I would let food go to waste because neither of us were willing to eat the leftovers.
Even just plain old water tasted like silicone in her cup.

construction_sents: I have always been a Huggies fan for little baby bums, and then switch to Up n Up brand to cut costs in the later years.

I was glad to find some Pampers in size 7 to try because my 3 year old is definitely still in diapers for nap and bedtime.

I have never thought Pampers was soft enough for baby skin, but in size 7 I must say I actually like them.

The designs are very cute and colorful, we have had no leaks through the night and the tabs are strong and hold up well with a rambunctious toddler.

The price and papery feel to the diapers means they merit 4 stars only.
However, since my child is older I don’t mind the rougher feel of the diapers because I’m just glad we have something sturdy to last us through all the failed potty training!
I use Aveeno baby on my kids, and this is a very similar product.
It works well to help alleviate the itching which my kids have so much of in the dry winter months.
The scent is ok - not as good as Aveeno, but not unpleasant.
This is an excellent alternative - at a very reasonable price.

The product arrived with no instructions on how to put it together, although the included papers listed all the parts and all the descriptions were in barely decipherable English.

After adjusting the height to our toilet seat, the potty did not sit securely on it and felt wobbly.
My child found it difficult to climb up and then turn around to sit while balancing on the step, which is not very wide and ends up being positioned under the toilet bowl edge.
The handles are definitely a necessity.
Potty training is still in progress so we will see how it fares in the long run.
For the price, I would skip this one and find another brand for a step potty seat.

We have been team Huggies since the start until we switched to the much-cheaper and still functional Up n Up (Target brand) when our toddler was big enough that the cost of diapers was really adding up.
/>I am trying Pampers for our second baby.

So far, I haven’t been convinced.
These are the Swaddlers which is Pampers’ softer version of diapers, comparable to Huggies Little Snugglers.

Pros:

The back of the diaper goes quite high up baby’s back which is good for containing blowouts.
2.

No evidence of causing our baby a rash.

Cons:
1.
I absolutely hate the inner lining of this diaper.
It is kind of a weird mesh that always sticks to my baby’s bum and I have to see it peel off when I remove his diaper, even when there is no poop involved.

It looks gross to me.
2.
There were a lot of pee leaks when we first started using them; I thought it was because baby was still transitioning into size 2 from size 1 diapers.

But a few weeks later, he is still more likely to have a leak with these diapers after an hour or two, rather than Pampers baby dry or Huggies Little Snugglers.
3.

More papery feel to diaper compared to huggies Little Snugglers which are softer.
They are also mostly a plain white if you prefer a print/pattern on diapers.
4.
They cost more but have been less functional for us in comparison to other brands.
I absolutely adore this lovey for my baby.
My first had a bunny as well from Ikea which was light and cotton, but honestly had kind of creepy eyes.
I love this bunny so much better with its gentle sleeping eyes and the oh-so adorable way it clutches the blanket.
That detail alone makes it a step above all the other loveys which are essentially animal heads floating on top of tiny blankets.
/>The assortment of colors are beautiful - different from the typical baby blue/pink/gray, there is no differentiation based on your child’s gender.
It is soft and fluffy and washes well.

The colors are so pretty and striking that we are using it as a prop in our baby’s monthly photos until baby is old enough to safely sleep with it on his own.
I haven’t been able to find a security blanket of this size for this price from anywhere.
Buy this or one of the other cute designs like the koala.
Battat has quickly become one of our favorite baby/toy brands.

We have been team Huggies since the start until we switched to the much-cheaper and still functional Up n up (target brand) when our toddler was big enough that the cost of diapers was really adding up.
I am trying Pampers for our second baby.

So far, I haven’t been convinced.
These are the Pampers Baby Dry diapers which are comparable to Huggies Snug & Dry.

Pros:

When I make sure to put the tabs tight enough, there are rarely any leaks.
2.

This is a huge 200+ diapers box which you definitely will need in size 1.

Cons:
1.

They have a much more papery feel than the comparable Huggies in the same size.
2.
They have a nice powdery scent on their own.
But the scent usually makes it impossible for me to tell by smell if baby has pooped or not (EBF baby).

And added scent likely means more chemicals.
3.
Why put tiny yellow dandelions in the print right near the leg cuffs?!
At a glance it always looks like baby’s poo has leaked out, then I have to investigate if that is truly the case or is it just the print.

This seems like a small thing but it is annoying when you are changing diapers several times in the day and night and don’t need that kind of confusion.
4.
The pictures show baby Ernie and Bert which we didn’t get in our box of diapers.
/>Based on these cons and the cost per diaper as compared to other standard brands, I don’t recommend these diapers.
Soft, 100% cotton, neutral color and (somewhat boring) design pattern.
They washed and dried easily and fit snugly on the full size Graco pack n play mattress that comes with the crib.

/>Taking one star off only because of the price - there are numerous 2-pack sheet options available for pack n plays that are much less in price, which are also made of soft cotton and have great prints.
It's the perfect mattress for a toddler bed.
I like that it's not too "crinkly" sounding, like other infant/toddler mattresses can be.
It is firm and lightweight.
It's light enough that it's very easy to change sheets.
It's not thick enough for the kids to be able to jump on the bed, but they have other beds in the house for that :)

I'm writing this review because I am extremely impressed with this toy chest.
Firstly, the parts and instructions were laid out so beautifully - making it very easy to assemble.

It still took some time, but that's because this is a quality product.
It is made of real wood, not cardboard/plywood/whatever cheap materials others may use.

This wood is beautifully painted.
All in all, an excellent product that I'm very glad I purchased.
This is a typical Johnson & Johnson kids' shampoo.
It's more or less tear free, but not completely - if it gets in the kids' eyes, there is a little irritation - but it's less irritation than it would be with a different shampoo.
The scent is not too overpowering, so that's good.
My daughter's hair actually gets fewer knots with this shampoo than with others.
I love the light lavender, calming scent of this baby shampoo.
Like the other no more tears products, this does not burn the eyes if it gets in.
I use it on my kids as both a shampoo and a body wash.
I live this lotion, but I'm confused by the name.
I'm not sure what they mean by cotton touch.
It has a very light fragrance, and a lovely, creamy texture.
It feels perfect for tiny baby skin.
We put it on the mattress, underneath the bed sheet, and it doesn't slip.
It's soft and plush, and stays in place.
It's high enough that it keeps my daughter from falling out of bed, but not so high that she has trouble getting in.
It fits the twin size bed perfectly, but can be cut down for a toddler bed if needed.
I love that there are not too many parts, and that all of them are dishwasher safe.
It's very easy to clean, and looks super cute.
For the price, this is a great set of 10 magnetic drawer/cabinet locks.
They were easy to install on our bedroom dresser drawers and kitchen cabinets to keep out curious babies.
They worked as expected to close off outlets.
We got a good amount of bubbles in the bath, but it also required a decent amount of liquid to get them (just the 2 capfulls were not sufficient).
The scent is strong, but not bad.
My daughter's skin did seem a little dry after using this in her bath, so I applied a good amount of lotion after.

These chubby little utensils are perfect for chubby little hands to grip.
They are super cute :)
like that the part that the kids eat from is metal and not plastic.
I also do like the raised design - it works - keeping the spoon and fork off the table.

I also like that they are dishwasher safe.
The
only thing I don't like is that they are bulky, and as such take up a lot of room in my utensil drawer.
They're a lot bulkier than other baby spoons and forks I've tried.
Not the most durable bag, and also not as large as expected.
I used it for my Summer Infant 3D Lite stroller - the wheels still stuck out.
I actually don't mind that part.
But the material is flimsy, I don't expect it to last very long.
The good thing about it though is that it keeps the stroller covered and secure - less likely to snag on something and break during transit or in the gate check process.
This straw cup is very durable - it has stood up to the many drops and falls that my rambunctious toddler has already put it through.

The button is easy to push.
Cleaning is easy - it's dishwasher safe with not too many parts.
It has the bottle, the lid, the straw and the valve, which are easy to remove and also put back in.

I use a dishwasher basket for the valve; the straw I just slip onto one of the stems of the top rack of the dishwasher.
The hook in the lid is also very helpful - it makes it easier for my kids to pull the bottle out of the side pocket of their backpacks.
Overall, this is a great car seat.

I really love the Graco brand, which has served our family well.
The car seat was not too difficult to install, except for one specific part: the bottom buckle for the 5-point harness.
Try as I might, I was unable to adjust this to a more comfortable fit.

My husband and I spent about 15 minutes on it, and were absolutely not able to get it to budge.

That is the only issue I had with this car seat.
It was easy to set up in the car, and my daughter is comfortable in it.
I like that it has dual cup holders, which are very convenient.

We've had many leaks already
- they run large, so are a loose fit for my almost 3 year old
- the material is a little papery, and seems less comfortable than Huggies.

This may actually be a little useful while actively potty training, but not necessarily.

Overall, they're cute but not effective for us.
I've been a big fan of the Graco brand for years.
I have gotten the 4 in 1 car seat for both my kids - and even for my nephew.
I love knowing I won't have to buy another car seat.
The seat is comfortable, the buckle is easy to open and close, and to tighten.
It has 2 cupholders, which I've found few car seats do.
All around a great car seat.
Very gentle, did not irritate my kids' skin.
I also like that it is fragrance free.
This potty seat is lightweight and, as advertised, is convenient for .
It is non slip.
Just a couple of points to note.
Firstly, it does have a ring to hang on a hook but does not come with a potty hook.
You can buy those separately for about 3 or 4 dollars.
Also, the splash guard is a little lower than on other seats we use.
These are very cute diaper pants.
I love the designs.

They also seem to be comfortable and I haven't seen any more leaks than with other brands we've tried.
However, they are significantly more expensive.
I don't see that much more value in these than in say Pull Ups.
This makes travel so much more convenient.
It is easy to install and use, and of course very portable.
However, it is not as comfortable as a full booster, so my child is not a fan for longer distances.
Being fans of Huggies throughout most of our diapering journey, I was interested to try Pampers in size 6 since we never liked Pampers for our newborn.

The reason being they felt more papery and weren't as soft as Huggies.

The size of these diapers is quite spacious and my 1 year old is still growing into them so we've saved most for a couple of months later.
Since he is older, neither of us minded them being less soft and they didn't leave marks against his skin.
He did not get a diaper rash from them and we experienced no leaky diapers or (thankfully!)
blowouts so they do the job well.
For the slightly higher price compared to our regular diaper purchase, I don't intend to buy more of Pampers
but I know plenty of parents who love them and use them exclusively so they are popular for a reason

I really like that J&J is reformulating with safer ingredients.
This lotion is not the same as the original product, and I don't expect it to be.
It is thinner, and has a lighter and different scent, but it still moisturizes well.
The bottle came with the pump taped down to prevent leaking.
It arrived in perfect condition.
This lotion does a great job of keeping skin soft and moisturized without feeling greasy.
It has a very light scent, which I prefer over the heavy perfume of the original lotion.
/>I just don't understand what function cotton provides as an added ingredient.
Is this just marketing, or does it actually provide a real benefit?

You are provided the bassinet and the seat, but you'll have to choose which option you'll need to attach to the frame.
You are provided sun canopy wires and clamps, but that is a separate option/purchase.
You are provided a rain cover, but is only usable if you have the separate canopy.

Our chronological journey with nose suckers/aspirators...

•
Nose Frida -- Because everyone apparently knows about this brand/item and recommends it.
At first, it's was a lifesaver, and it helped suck out snot very effectively.
Automatic/electric nose aspirators -- In an ideal world, these would be very convenient.
We've tried a couple of different brands, but the suction power on both of them was not very powerful (which essentially makes this ineffective for stubborn colds).
Additionally, there's more cleanup because of the additional intricate parts that are involved.

They also need to be charged or used with batteries and are typically quite expensive...2.5 stars.

• Off-brand manual nasal suckers -- Because the electric pumps were such a letdown, we went back to manual mouth-sucking pumps.
We found a couple generic brand versions that were essentially Nose Fridas, but less expensive, and occasionally, more effective.

The biggest issue continued to be the mouth sucking, which eventually would make us catch the cold as well or at least give us hoarse throats...4 stars.

•
This hand-pump nose aspirator --
Initially, we were a bit skeptical because it was so large, and the round nose head wasn't the best shape to be comfortably placed on the nose.
However, after several tries, this was by far the best option.
The manual hand pump delivers a consistent and strong suction (it really, really sucks well).
You do not need to use your mouth, so you avoid spreading germs.
Clean-up is quite easy because you only need to clean the nose part (not the pump).
There are a couple minor downsides though.
One, you may need at least 2 people to use this on your baby/toddler because the design of the nose tip doesn't allow an easily securable position on your kid's nose, and they will likely squirm.
Additionally, it's a bit more pricey than the other manual pumps, but in all honesty, this item is so effective, I think it's worth it...4.5 stars.

First of all, our household practices baby-led weaning, so meals tend to get a bit messy.
While these mats don't solve the mess problem, they are extremely useful to have around when eating out with a little one.
My toddler likes to pick things up, so it helps that these placemats are flat and stick to the table (there are 5 adhesive strips on the back, but you probably don't need to use all of them).
The 12 by 18 inch size is large enough for "most" meals, and the placemats also come with stickers, which help to occupy my toddler while we wait for food.
Afterwards, you can just roll up the placemat and throw everything away, making clean up fairly easy.
It's probably not as environmentally friendly as a reusable tray, but these disposables are just so convenient (and they are extremely portable, unlike the bulky trays).
So these placemats are not the perfect solution, but they are quite useful.

My baby gets a good oil rubdown after bath every night, and I've tried many different brands of baby oil.
I've used the generic Johnson's, which is a greasy mess, and I've tried small organic brands, which are lovely, but quite pricey.
Pipette was my go-to for awhile, but the bottle always leaked and got really oily, so I felt that I was wasting a quarter of the bottle.
Regarding this Colief brand, I love the lavender scent.

My toddler didn't get any rashes or allergic reactions, and I've used this for a week now.
I also think the cost is very reasonable considering the amount of oil in the bottle.
BUT... one big problem for me is the dispenser.
It just doesn't come out well!
I ended up just taking out the plastic spout and pouring directly from the bottle because the spout only dispenses one drop of oil at a time.
Who the heck invented this?
It is way too much work to prevent making a mess when I'm juggling a naked baby who is running around, impatiently waiting for me to finish doing whatever after-bath routine mama needs to do.
I have zero complaints about the quality of the baby oil.
It feels and smells great!
Please just change your bottling!
I've never been a huge fan of baby wipes because they are usually not environmentally friendly, and the preservatives aren't great for a baby's skin.
However, it's difficult to avoid using them because they are extremely convenient.
So I'm glad that this brand used plant-based ingredients.
I also like that these are unscented, and the material is a bit textured, which makes it easier to wipe messes off.
However, these wipes contain citric acid, and I would prefer not to use them on my baby's face.
I think water and a clean, soft towel is the best for a baby's face, but I know that's not always possible, especially when I'm on the go.

Additionally, I wish the company was more transparent about where these were made, but seeing that my eczema-prone baby has not had any negative reaction to these wipes, I'm generally happy with them.
As my toddler is getting more and more curious about things around the house, I noticed his particular interest in shutting doors, so I've been getting worried that he would hurt his fingers.
These Nutjam pinch guards work great because they are extremely easy to put on and take off.

At daycare, my baby recently started sleeping on a cot, so they also requested a thin blanket for him to use during those nap times.

However, I am not a fan of the pillow...it is too thick and clunky for a toddler, and it's a bit awkward to roll up.
Overall though, I'm generally happy with this item because my toddler seems to like laying down on the blanket.
Because I really loved the Pigeon brand foam body wash, I wanted to try other products from them.

Initially I was concerned that the bottle was quite small, and that the oil itself was really watery (I apply a lot of oil on my baby because of his eczema, and I'm accustomed to thick oils that really grease up my baby's skin).
However, after using this, I found that the oil absorbs quickly.
Admittedly, I do use a lot more oil compared to other brands that I've tried, but I really like that this Pigeon one is unscented, light, and gentle.
I don't mind applying a little more because the price seems reasonable.
I estimate that this one bottle will last me about 4-6 weeks, assuming that I apply it all over my baby's body every night.
The only feature that I'm not too thrilled about is the actual dispenser, which is a bit unique because the oil shoots out in a very thin, stream-like opening.

It takes more time and effort than I would prefer, but I understand that it was probably designed this way because of how watery this oil is (there would probably be a lot of leakage issues if a pump dispenser was used).
So far, I'm a fan!
I love Japanese skincare products, but this is the first time I tried a Japanese baby product.
And despite being a Japanese item, I was still surprised that there weren't any instruction or usage translations in English.
But I was told that Pigeon was a trustworthy brand, so I gave it a try.
The foam comes out smooth with a nice, airy texture, and it's easy to apply on large surface areas with just one pump.
I typically only use about 4 pumps in total for my baby's entire body (I'm not quite sure how many pumps the bottle will produce, but I feel it's worth the price).
I absolutely love that it's unscented, and it does not dry my baby's skin.
I also like that I don't have to rub too vigorously since the product is already foamy.
I'm very satisfied, and I have already recommended this bath wash to many of my parent friends!
I'm always looking for good sippy cups for my toddler, and the shape of this Mum to Mum brand is similar to my Philips Avent brand one, but much more affordable.
My toddler doesn't seem to mind this one, and he drank water from it fine, but I don't like the flimsy handles because it spins and doesn't lock in place.

Aesthetically, this is a very elegant-looking high chair, so I'm hoping to use it more effectively when my toddler gets older, but for now, back to our Graco.

I originally bought this to put under my toddler's high chair while he's eating (because he often throws food on the floor), but I also ended up using it as a splat mat for our finger painting activities.

Unfortunately, I did notice that the non-toxic paint we used stained the splat mat, and we couldn't fully get it off (on most hard surfaces, just a simple wipe with a wet rag works).
Other than that, it's been really useful for us to have, and I definitely think it helps to have one if you also have a messy toddler!
The overall body fit is great (I ordered the 12-24 months, and my toddler is 14 months old), and the elastic material of the cuffs around the ankles and wrists are thick and soft.

/>My toddler has worn this a few times now, but I'm still looking for other PJs/sleep sacks with softer material.
In general though, this is an attractive and comfortable enough set of PJs.
In general, I am practicing baby-led weaning.
Occasionally though, if I want to feed my baby some soup or if I need to scoop up some of the leftovers on his plate that are too cumbersome for him to hold, I need to use a spoon.
The beginner silicone-based infant spoons I've used were great initially, but now, they are too small to hold adequate substance, so I graduated to these utensils.
These attractive little utensils are now the perfect size for that substantial soup slurp.
Even though my baby can't properly use spoons/forks yet, he still loves to hold them.
Because they are rounded off, the forks aren't immediately dangerous for my baby.
Also, he loves to bang them on his tray, which can get quite loud, but these utensils don't make quite as loud as a sound as standard non-baby ones.
So overall, I'm satisfied with this order, and I look forward to when he can actually use these effectively.

It’s thought to be the result of lingering hormones from mom, which is why sometimes (not always)

we see it with babies who also have “baby acne,” which is also caused by hormones.

I use grapeseed oil for infant massage.
(Grapeseed is a good choice, in case it gets on baby’s hands which end up in their mouth, out of caution in case they have a nut allergy… in lieu of other oils.

And you never want to use olive oil, ever.)

So, I used my fingers and rubbed grapeseed oil into his scalp while he laid on a towel.
I let it sit for about 20 minutes, then bathed him.
I used babyganics shampoo.
I washed his hair with the shampoo twice, using the soft bristled side of the brush.
It still left a little oil residue, but not too much.
After bath, while nursing, I used the awesome comb and some gentle pressure to scrape the softened and loosened skin from his forehead and scalp.
It’s amazing how much this pulls up.
/>I did this for a long time, about 20 minutes, slowly and gently.
I was careful to not break the skin or pull anything that wasn’t ready to be removed.
A little bit of hair came with it, but we didn’t get any bald spots.

Some treatments and other topicals may cause more temporary hair loss.

He was left with some flakes I couldn’t quite get, but overnight they came off and the next AM he looked much better.
I shampood (no more oil) the second night using the sponge and the soft bristles in small circles and in different directions.
I rinsed and repeated the scraping with the comb after bath.
There was much less to get this time.

Today is day three and it looks nearly gone!

Once
it’s all gone, I’ll continue using the brush set to prevent future “cradle crap.”

If you buy (like we have) this Little Remedies product, then you probably also buy their saline spray.

Only you know what's best for your child, trust your gut.

my Little Remedies Saline Review:
These drops have been amazing for us, BUT, WE JUST FOUND WHAT APPEARS TO BE BLACK MOLD GROWING IN THEM!!!!
We have purchased probably 25 of these bottles (one for each room, diaper bag, car, etc... and replenished as ran out over the last 18 months).
Our daughter has used these since she came home from the hospital alongside our trusty Nose Frida.
It was a winning combination, until we looked under the cap and noticed what appears to be black mold growing in two  of our open bottles!

WHAT?!?!

I'm enclosing pictures, so please check yours.
I'll write the company and report back on their reply.
For what it's worth,  we use them exactly as directed.
The instructions say to wipe clean after each use, which we do.
We are also mindful to not release the 'squeeze" until it's well away from our baby's face (meaning, we're being careful not to suction anything INTO the bottles.)
They bottles never come away from her nose with boogies on them, which is to say, these findings are not things that have come out of her nose, but bacteria/mold/?
from inside the bottle.

To further support our efforts to keep baby safe and her products sterile, after EVERY single use, we wash (with soap & water) her aspirator, and then ALSO, run it through an electric steam sterilizer.
We're not sloppy with our child's hygiene, so we are mortified.
Just trying to help fellow mommies & daddies out there - CHECK YOUR BOTTLES!

This happens whether it's opened or closed - and, it's continuous.
Specifically, it will slowly drain itself!

The fat content gives the milk 'legs' (of sorts) allowing it to creep up the straw.

These cups leak stinky milk all over everything!

The mobile is a little flimsy and doesn't like to stay in place as the infant is swinging.
The highest swing setting on this swing seems way too extreme (I agree with other reviewers on this one!).
The swing sits deep, so we weren't able to use this when our infant was first born (7 pounds) but now that she's bigger she is able to sit comfortably.

All in all, we enjoy this swing and our infant seems to love swing time.

construction_sents: Lullaby Instrumental, Ocean Waves, Heartbeat, and White Noise are the 4 sounds.

I have tried and tested 8 different Video Baby Monitors....looking for one that meets ALL my needs.
Its a daunting and at times frustraighting task...
but I finally found one that checks off all the boxes!!!

This VTech VM343 system!

Pros:

>* Easy to set up right out of box!
* Clear Camera Picture in Daylight!
* Excellent Night Vision - Clear Picture!
* Excellent Night Vision - Range.

Can see entire 12x15 room from top to bottom very clearly in pitch blackness!
*

Great Range... reaches all round inside of my home and several hundred feet outside my home (which is very important to me!!!)
* Can add Additional Cameras - LOVE this feature.

Will come in handy if we are blessed with another baby!

Cons:
*
Loud Beeping whenever you change the volume on parent unit.
So if its 2am and you want to turn it down or up...it makes a Loud beep.
And no way to turn that off that I found.

So I just make sure the Volume is where I want it before bedtime.
*
The Outside Signal Range is only good IF you have the Antenna up.
Which means you cannot put it in your pocket while your are outside working...you'll actually need to sit it somewhere

so you can keep the Antenna up.
* Green "Power" light on Camera.
Right where child will notice it.
So I put black tape over it.
But you'd think manufactures would not put lights anywhere on the part that goes in the baby's room!
/>All in all I really like this system!!!
And like I said I've bought and tested and returned 8 different ones (well returned 7...
Kept this one :-) )
I have recommend this to ALL my mom friends and moms to be!!!!
/>Pro's of this Monitor:

* Easy to set up and start using
*

Great Night Vision...very Clear...Even in pitch black 12x16 room

Con's of this Monitor:
* POOR RANGE!
I live in a newer brick 1 story home.
I could not take 1 step out onto my back porch without it loosing signal.

Not sure if it would even work in a 2 story home!

Summary - If you are only wanting to monitor your child while you are inside your home...then this is a good choice.
Again the night vision was exactly what I was hoping for....but the poor poor range is not acceptable.
So I sent it back for full refund!
Now time to order another Monitor and see if it has these 2 features I need!!!
Terrible Range!!!!
Set up was easy and the camera was decent.
The night vision was just OK.
But again the Range was terrible!
We live in a new 1 story brick 2500sqft house with basement.
Camera was in room on North side of house....the "out of range" signal started as soon as I got to my Laundry room on the South side of my house - While still inside the house.
A good monitor should work perfectly inside the house and up to several hundred feet outside the house...in my humble opinion.
This is NOT that monitor!
So my search continues!!!
I was looking for a nice looking (non kid themed) toy organizer for our family room.
This storage unit works perfectly.
It goes with our rooms decor perfectly.
It's easy to assemble - hubby & I did it in 30mins.
It's solid & sturdy.
And It holds so many toys, books, stuffed animals, etc.

This portable potty seat (that goes on the big toilet) is the ONLY ONE I found that had a good sized Pee Guard for boys.

Not good when your out to dinner
and you get pee on the front of your shirt!!!!

I was looking for a backpack diaper bag that is big enough to hold a travel potty seat (the kind that you put on the big potty)..but not to big to make it hard or awkward to carry.

all in that main zipper compartment - where there are 2 large open pockets on either side (front and back) and 1 on the side.

It would be good if you still were using bottles too as it has 3 bottle size pockets on the back wall.

The Navy Blue color means that both myself and my hubby can carry it with no problems.
This bag fits my needs!
And if you too are in the potty learning stage and you need to carry potty seat with you everywhere you go....then THIS BAG is the one you want!!!!
Again it fits the potty seat we got (The Munchkin Grip Potty Training Seat) Perfectly!!!!
I was looking for a Small but Sturdy 2-Step Stool for my 2 Year old.
After searching and searching I decided on this one
and I'm glad I did.
It arrived in perfect new condition and the sticker was easy to peel off.
My toddler can easily carry it over to the sink to wash his hands.
The non-slip gray sections on both steps is a good thing!
Helps my son feel secure!
All in all its a good product at a good price.
Just what I was looking for!
After the diapers we had been using on our LO since birth were discontinued when he was 18 months old...I went on the search for new diapers.
After reading lots and lots of reviews I ordered a pack of Bambo size 4 diapers.
We've used them our boy for 6 months and then moved up to Size 5 diapers.
And I love that they have no toxins or chemicals to harm my baby!!!!
My only complaint is that the side tabs are not as thick (wide) nor as sturdy (not too stretchy) as our previous brand.
If they were about 1/2' wider and about Half Less Stretchy...they'd be perfect!!!!
Also I will note that the size listed on the packages (any size) seems way off.
For example, my 2 year old is 35"
Tall and only 25 Pounds....and the size 5 (which say they are for 26-49 pounds) is a joke because they are only a little bit too big on him....and again he's only 25 pounds.
So there is NO WAY they'd fit up to 49 pounds.
First, I will say that I have been in search of the perfect diaper bag for 3 years now....and sadly the search continues.
I bought this bag thinking that it would be big enough / organized enough to handle everything you need for a newborn/baby AND everything you need for a toddler.

I used this bag every single day for 2 weeks....here is my candid real life review:

PROS:
/>> I will say that this "diaper bag" does not look for feel like a traditional diaper bag.
It is very stylish and classy!!
Has the looks of a high-end designer handbag.
I did get several compliments from women when I was out.
/>>  Main Compartment Zipper Close.

So NOTHING falls out!

> Its great that it has 3 different carry options (i.e. Hand/Shoulder,
Crossbody, Backpack).

But seen Cons....

>

Its overall size is big enough to handle baby stuff and toddler stuff.....but see Cons....

CONS:

> There is not nearly enough organization inside of this bag to make it a great diaper bag.
I mean there are only 3 "pockets" inside this big bag.
On the back wall there are 2 open pockets that are big enough to fit a cell phone each...that's it.
And on the front wall of bag there is a zipper pocket.
The size of a normal cosmetic zipper pocket in most handbags.
So you have this big open space in which things will just lay on top of each other.
So I had to dig around and pull stuff out to find things that might have shifted to the bottom.

Not Good!

> I was excited for the backpack carry option.
But how you get the backpack straps is by using the long thin leather (no padding) crossbody strap as the backpack straps.
So while the bag is empty it feels fine.

But as soon as you fill the bag up with all you need....and it has weight to it...the leather straps dig into your underarm/shoulder and its not comfortable.

> The bag only comes in a very girly Melon color.
So my hubby would NOT touch this bag.

So that means we'd need to have 2 of everything to pack 2 bags with (one for him and one for me)...again NOT GOOD.

> No Metal Feet on the bottom of bag (to help keep it off the dirty floors).
/>So my ongoing search for the perfect functional diaper bag for two kids, that can be carried or worn like a backpack continues.
Simple 2 piece design with High Splash Guard (a Must for boys)!
My only suggestion is that the splash guard need to be concave or hallowed out instead of flat like it is so that the pee wont "bounce" off it back onto baby!
But I love the $9 price tag.
So I bought one for each bathroom!  :-)
I wanted a simple (no sounds or lights) potty seat for my toddler.
One that has good back support and adjustable height.
This one fits that well and my toddler sits on it comfortably all the time.
The main issue I have is if you are potty training a BOY...then the "pee shield" on this seat is way wrong!
Yes it comes up in front but it is Flat...instead of being Curved In or Concave.
So the pee will bounce right off of it and back on baby or his cloths.

This is the ONLY Non-Plastic Kids Snack Container that helps keep the snacks inside that I found (and I searched high and low).

I am very familiar with Huggies Pure & Natural Diapers as we've used them on our Son from Birth to now 18months.
I picked this exact diaper because of the Pure & Natural claim (i.e. no chemicals or toxins).
So I started with the Newborn size and am now at Size 4.
I have used HUNDREDS of this product
so I know exactly how they should be.
I've always bought them from my local Babies R Us store....
but since this line has now been Discontinued by Huggies....
I had to order from Amazon.
This was the reason I became a Prime Member because they are only available in the Prime Pantry Pack.

They Look and Feel the same as they always have....

I  mean its the same Brand,  Same Line, Same Packaging, Same Name, etc.

construction_sents: This bib is pretty cool and different from most typical bibs.
It definitely has more surface area and can catch more messes.
It looks well made and should hold up.
But, there are a couple quirks that make it not quite perfect for us.
First, the neck hole is pretty small, so fine for a very new eater but less so for a toddler.
Second, the patterned side goes on the inside which seems strange.
We also like to hose down the high chair and tray which we probably can’t do with the Velcro tabs attached.
I could see this working well for some young babies, but it’s not quite right for us.
I was really exited to see this alternative to silicone toddler plates as I feel like those absorb lots of smells and can make food taste different sometimes.
These wouldn’t have worked for me in the earlier days because my little one needed the suction bottom plates to not knock (or throw) her plate.
Now that she is a little older, these work well.

They are cute and look to be high quality.

A couple hesitations.
First, the texture is very weird to touch and gives both me and my husband shivers up our back (like nails on a chalkboard).

Second, the instructions say not to use with hot or acidic food… we usually serve hot lunch and dinner so I’m hoping they mean scalding hot versus just a warm meal, otherwise this plate isn’t very versatile!
These doorknobs don’t look like anything special but they work.
They are lightweight plastic and just pop together over your doorknobs.
I thought I might break the plastic pushing the halves together but it was fine.
These fit over my wider and flatter (hockey puck shaped) Emtek knobs, which I was a little worried about.
So far so good!
We can open them and my toddler cannot.
We put one on the inside door of her room so she cannot roam around outside her room at night.
I don’t think she’ll have the strength to open it for a while, but even if she did, I’m hopeful it would take her a long time and the plastic rattling would wake us up over the monitor.
I ordered this for my two year old
and she likes to use it.
She had no problem figuring out how it works.
It is generously sized unlike many other toddler cups, which I appreciate.
It also feels sturdy.
I assumed, however, that it would be leak proof.
Unfortunately it is not - if you turn it upside down, liquid will flow out.
I probably wouldn’t want to pack this in a bag for that reason.
But, this works as an at home cup for my daughter.
This is a good sippy cup at a good price from a trusted brand.
We received the purple color, which I was happy with.
It is very cute in its design.
I think this cup is a great transition from bottle to cup.
My daughter is a little beyond this stage at 2 and found this cup confusing because she usually uses straw cups.
This one has to be tipped up to fill the bottles nipple while drinking.
But I’m planning to use it for my younger one.
/>It doesn’t leak and is overall a solid sippy cup.

I loved the concept of these and the ability to keep the kitchen looking less messy without the locks that tie two cabinets together, BUT my toddler was able to pull at the cabinets enough for these to come off after just a month or so.
I think these would work better for a less determined toddler or younger baby just starting to explore!
My little one LOVED this teether
so I just ordered a second for her new sibling.
She seemed to get a bunch of relief while teething, and really gravitated towards this banana.
Since it is made of silicone, it is a breeze to keep clean and sanitary.
The strap is a great addition as it won't end up on the floor as much or get lost - just don't leave baby unattended with the strap!
I would highly recommend this teether toy for any baby in the 3month to 1 year (maybe even beyond) range, as it provides comfort and is a great way to get into good toothbrushing habits early!
These straps are great for attaching toys, teethers, or bottles to a high chair or stroller.
They prevent things from going flying when your little one is done with them.
The silicone is a breeze to wipe down if needed.
The sizing is adjustable so they can hold on to pretty much anything.
Just make sure not to leave baby unattended with these as they could be hazardous if baby got caught up in one.
My little one is a fan of both pouches and yogurt, so I figured this would be a hit.
My husband and I tried it and also agreed that it didn’t taste good (to us at least).
It’s pretty sour/unsweet, and has a flavor profile that’s different to most yogurt pouches or tubes.
We have never tried nido milk powder, so perhaps just aren’t used to it.
Unfortunately, these weren’t a hit for us!
If you have tried nido milk powder and like the taste, perhaps give these a try!
It’s great to be able to provide yogurt and calcium that doesn’t have to be stored in the fridge with short expiration times.
These liners work well in our travel potty and save us from having to fully clean out the potty each time our toddler goes.
They feel thin but we’ve found them to be strong enough and they haven’t leaked for us.
They are priced well.
This potty is great for on-the-go.
We aren’t quite ready for that stage yet, but we plan to keep it in the car for potty emergencies as it’s super compact.
It’s not quite sturdy/substantial enough for our liking for home potty training use, but my toddler has used it a few times at home and it works well enough.
It seems to fit most brands of liners, if you want to use those and not clean it out each time.
I was excited about the idea of a touch less thermometer for my toddler now that she’s outgrown the need for the rectal thermometer only.
I’ve found this particular design a little tricky because the thermometer, it’s beeping and it’s red light all seem to scare her
so she won’t sit still for it.
So, I’m finding it tough to get an accurate measurement because of holding it the correct distance from her forehead.
Of course, this would be the same for any similar thermometer - I just hoped for an easier experience.
On adults, I have no complaints and this has worked well.
Hopefully we can use it more when she’s a tiny bit older!
We have a fancy sleep sack for our daughter that is super soft and temperature regulating, but were looking for a basic back up option for when that sack needs to be in the wash.
This one fits the bill!
Is the quality similar?
No, but it's a fraction of the price.
This is a basic cotton sack with no frills.
It's not uncomfortable at all - it feels like an inexpensive cotton t-shirt that you'd get with a brand's logo on it, but it's not luxuriously soft.
It's exactly what I needed and I think the price is right.
The sizing seems about right too.
The 12-18m works well for my 17 month old, with a little extra room.
This wooden baby toy is a really nice addition to any nursery.
It’s not overly bright or plastic-y so looks timeless and can blend into any decoration scheme.
It’s great for little ones having floor time, as the hanging toys can keep them entertained for a while.
The design is cute, gender neutral, and it looks to be well made.
This would make a nice gift too.
These bibs are super convenient for on the go.
They are extremely lightweight and fold up very small
so we always keep a couple in our diaper bag for any impromptu eating away from home.
They are perfect for restaurants or friends houses, where you don’t want to have to pack and then wash a reusable one.
These have little stickies to stay in place; and a pouch to catch food.
It isn’t quite as effective as a normal bib, but it does the job well enough!
The design is cute too!
I received this baby gate but still haven't installed it one month later because it didn't come with screws, I haven't had a chance to go get some, and the installation seems VERY involved.
My husband and I aren't particularly handy, so I'm a little concerned we will not be able to do it correctly.
I'm also not sure that the gate will  restrain our boisterous 1.5 year old effectively.

She is very good at figuring out buckles, zippers, latches, and the material seems a little flimsy, so I'm worried that we will go through the trouble of putting it up and drilling holes in our walls, and then it won't serve its purpose.
I may try to find something a little more user-friendly, or get someone in to help.
My daughter is 15 months old and we have always kept a couple pouches in our diaper bag for easy and healthy-ish snacks when we are out and about.
I was attracted to these as I know Holle makes great quality products, and because we don't get much beet in my daughter's diet otherwise and variety is always good.
She seemed to like these pouches and sucked them right down without hesitation.
I tried a little and found the flavor pleasant but definitely earthy (beets).

The consistency is noticeably thinner than other pouches in our rotation (and is described as "juice", which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but could lead to more spills/squirts if a younger baby is self-feeding.

My only concern here is the price.
I understand that these are "clean" and organic, and made in Europe, but at $3 per pouch, this still seems very high for pretty inexpensive ingredients (mostly apple and banana).
Other organic pouches at our grocery store or online are about half the price.
We did enjoy these but most likely wouldn't order them again at full price.
These bibs are pretty similar to other silicone bibs we have for our daughter, but the price point and quality particularly impressed us.
They are a little thicker than others we have, which I think will mean that they last longer and won't break down.
The colors are muted and the patterns are subtle and cute.
I think they are gender neutral.
I find these easy to clean with a little warm water and dish soap - much easier than having to machine wash fabric ones!
I was excited to try this snack tray as my daughter’s stroller just has a bar and no tray, and she loves to snack on the go.
I intended to use this with our Uppababy Vista, as the product is described as a universal fit.
Unfortunately, the tray sits weirdly high on our stroller so it’s hard for her to get her arms up to the snacks because they are at chest level against her body.
Maybe it would work for a taller or bigger child.
I probably just need to spend the money and get the official tray for her stroller, but thought this was a great idea to try first.
Our other stroller is the YoYo, but since that doesn’t have a handlebar, we can’t use this with that stroller either.
This moisturizer is great for sensitive baby or adult skin.
It’s fragrance free and has all clean ingredients.
I have been using this on both my one year old daughter and myself - both of us have light eczema - and it’s been wonderful for both of our skin.
It’s pretty thin but works nicely to lock in moisture after a shower/bath and doesn’t leave the skin sticky.
The pump bottle works well and the branding looks nice.
It’s pricey for a moisturizer, but if you or your baby has sensitive skin, it will probably be comparable in price or maybe a little cheaper than other high end products that would also work for you.
Highly recommend and would buy with the other products in this line as a gift bundle!
These disposable placemats are a great idea for busy moms when eating out with kids.
We can just stick one down to the restaurant table and not get food everywhere or worry about disinfecting the table.
Then at the end, you just roll it up, containing all the mess, and throw it out.
At $.25 per mat at the current pricing, these are great to just keep in a diaper bag for whenever they may be needed.
It doesn’t hurt that the design is cute and can keep out little one interested for a little while.
/>My only complaint is that the glue tabs can leave residue on the table.
I am not overly concerned about this in a restaurant, but would feel bad if I used these at a friend or family members house and got glue on their table.

Our daughter is only 13 months so we still mostly use side tab diapers but we’re excited to try the “pants” (aka pull ups) to see if they made diaper changes any easier now that she wrestles us every time!
She’s a size 3 in most big brand diapers, though may be sizing up to a 4 soon.
The Large in these “pants” fit very well and have extra room for growth.

Here are my thoughts:

Pros
these pants make diaper changes SO MUCH EASIER.

This is true for all pull-ups I assume, but this is our first time using non tab diapers and it’s a game changer when they are so squirmy.
-

these have a blue line indicator
-

they have a little tab on the back that unfolds and has adhesive, so the used diaper can be rolled up and secured before throwing out
-
they are pretty cute and gender neutral without any trends (Disney etc).

They do say “I love mom and dad”, which could be a negative for single parent or two mom/dad families.
-

the elastic allows for a very secure fit that keeps everything closed in even when baby is very active, without being overly constrictive.
-
they seem pretty absorbent.

They aren’t quite as good as our go to overnight diapers (Huggies little movers), but about the same as other big name diapers for day time use.

Cons
- the price.
At the time of this review, these are $0.85 a diaper which is a lot.
This is more than some of the most premium brands like Coterie, around double many name brands like pampers and Huggies, and quadruple many generic brands.
These do seem like nice quality but I’m not sure I could justify the price, especially given that they aren’t as absorbent for overnight as others we’ve tried.
We don’t have a regalo playard but recently got a babyseater hexagonal playard so took a chance on this mat and it happens to be a great fit.
There is a tiny extra bit of fabric at the sides (maybe an inch) but it’s not noticeable and the bottom of the pad has a rubberized surface
so it doesn’t really slide around.

It makes me feel a lot better about leaving my little one in her playard unattended while I use the restroom or am cooking because she toppled over a lot and the playard doesn’t have any padding built in.
little one seems to like it, and I like the design and look of it so no complaints there.
It feels like a thick quilted blanket so it’s not super springy or padded but definitely cushions a fall if you have hard floors.
/>It could also be used without a playard simply as a mat for tummy time or playing outside.
The fabric isn’t water resistant, but the product does say that it is machine washable.
/>One of the product pictures on this page shows a baby using this as a mattress to sleep on with a hat and a blanket.
This is all kinds of unsafe - if you add a pad to a playard that didn’t come with it, it‘s not a regulated safe sleep space any more.
The pad is great for daytime play, but remove it before any naps or sleeps if that’s what you use the playard for!
We have been using this oil on our little one for a couple weeks now and really like it.
We usually use it right after her baths to help lock in some moisture as she naturally has dry-ish skin and some eczema patches that flare up if we don’t moisturize consistently.
This oil is beautifully packaged, looks and feels luxurious, and has worked well for our daughter’s skin.
It has a faint coconut smell from the coconut oil, but it doesn’t linger very long.
We really like it and are happy to be using such clean ingredients on her skin.

We have a "lawn" type drying rack in our house, which we love, but came across this product and decided to try it out for my parents' house, where we spend a lot of time with our daughter.
The rack comes in a cardboard box and is easy to assemble in a matter of seconds - you just poke the four twigs (?) into the base.

Overall, the product looks cute and fun, and appears to be well made (although one of our twigs was slightly dented).

The base has two layers - the tray, which catches water, and the upper layer that holds the twigs and rests on top of the tray.

They layers don't really snap together or anything, so while it's sturdy enough for the most part, if you knock the drying rack, they may separate and fall.

The twigs have slightly different configurations so can be assembled however works best for you in terms of the direction they face, colors etc.

We've found that the taller hook works well for bottles and the lower hook works well for the corresponding bottle lids/nipples.

The material of the base and twigs is a hard plastic.
This makes it easy to wipe down or wash, without any fear of anything getting stuck or growing on it.

On the downside, this means that the upper tray area is sleek and slippery so you cannot easily "rest" items there to dry if they don't fit on the hooks.

Overall, it's working well for cups and I like how easy it is to keep clean.
However, it's definitely less versatile than our "lawn" type rack - there is nowhere to put baby spoons, straws, medicine syringes or other small items that get washed.
So, I'd probably only recommend it for an older baby with mostly milk/water/juice cups being washed.

I bought these to use in my diaper genie elite and while the cartridges fit perfectly, I am less than thrilled with the bags themselves.
The plastic is not as thick as in the playtex refill cartridges and as a result the diaper genie itself smells.
Every time I open the diaper genie to remove the bag (or open the top to drop in a new diaper) the stink from the diapers in the pail permeates my son's room.
While there was some stench with the original refills, it was no where near as bad.
Since I hate throwing product away I will keep using these until they are all gone, but I will be going back to the original.

Good quality wood, nice finish, and overall very nice design details.
-

Color of pieces is even throughout, and upholstered sections are a nice touch to a room with the right color palette.
-

Relatively easy to assemble, except for mattress platform (see "Cons").
-

Feet are short/low to the floor, which makes it ideal for a toddler conversion, and for shorter people to access baby, rather than reaching up and over rails like other taller cribs.

Cons:

-
Extremely difficult to put mattress platform into crib during assembly.
Platform didn't reach holes in frame by 2 inches, so we had to bend/force mattress frame to fit.

Will have to do this every time you adjust the mattress height.
-

Feels closed in with no slats on head and foot of crib, instead of slats all the way around crib, which feels more open (previous crib had open slats).
-

Curved and solid foot and head boards prevents attachment of mobiles along these edges, as well as attachment of rail guards/cushions for babies who may chew along crib rail (like our kid!).
-

Upholstered cushioning on head and foot boards would be better inside crib as padding, rather than on exterior for design purposes only.

Overall, a very nice crib for the right nursery, but lacks certain practical elements, such as the ability to attach a mobile.

bedtime bath -- this is a bubble bath without much of the bubbles.

We wanted something large to put in the middle of the room so our baby could explore without picking up any little things that our older kids are constantly leaving on the floor.
At first, this seemed like a great solution.

However, we quickly started to notice some major problems with it.

PROS:
most mesh play yards, this one sits on the floor, so there is no weight limit.
That makes it easy for older siblings or adults to sit with the baby.
It also means you can place toys in it that you could not place in a raised playpen, such as a small activity table.
mesh is superior to other play pens in terms of visibility.
It’s astonishing easy to see thought from a distance.

Photographs through the mesh even come out well.

It is also very easy to fold.
It really does only take a few seconds to open and close.
It is really light, making it easy to carry with one hand.
It also folds down very small, not much bigger than a camping chair.
All of this makes it easy to take on the go, if that is something that matters to you.

/>CONS:

The biggest issue is that the square footage is essentially a lie.
It is (poorly) designed so that the floor of the playpen doesn’t actually start touching the ground until over a foot in.

It says 62” wide, and the frame is, but the only usable space is the center— about a 3ft diameter.

The cover is also miserable to get on and off.
The 16 snaps and 8 Velcro straps are a breeze.
However, the 8 backpack-style straps are a huge pain.
Literally, I have a sore shoulder after having to painstaking thread them in, hold them taught, and thread them back out again.
Surely there was a better way to design in?!
/>It has a 90-day warranty, but we didn’t even make it 90 days before seams started popping and mesh started tearing.
I saw other reviews about theirs breaking, but I figured they used it for travel or took it down often, allowing more wear and tear.
We put it up once and never took it down or moved it.
No one messes with it.
We just get the baby in and out a few times a day.
Our baby is not even old enough to walk and just learned to pull up to standing— which she can’t even do in this because the sides are too high— so she didn’t rip holes in the mesh, either.

It just isn’t as “durable” as it claims.

Finally, is claims it’s easy to clean, but it is NOT machine washable & does NOT wipe clean.
And trying to take the cover off to spot clean it in the sink would be like trying to spot clean a tent, a fitted king sheet, or a 1pc couch cover.
It’s cumbersome at best.
It should not be advertised as washable or “easy to clean”.
It is, however, easy to stain.
The main selling point for me was that it looked like the mat under it snapped on and off.
it does not come off at all.
I also gave them the benefit of the doubt when it came to reviews that the velcro scratched babies.

I took the time to make sure that each velcro tab was secure straight and firm, but after 10 minutes or so, the material (I wouldn't even say fabric b/c it's very plastic-y) had pulled down and exposed the scratchy velcro, sure enough.

Original review -
It was great as an individual camera but when you added the 2nd camera it brought about many glitches making it pretty bad.

Here are the pros & cons we found so far...

Cons: 
- IR bulbs on the camera shine red like a ring of creepy devil eyes, may scare a child...
my toddler says it kinda scared him during his nap
but he knew it was a new camera so that helped but it took him a few days to get used to it.

Also there is a large green light on the camera (the on/off button) - we are from the school of thought the cameras should be invisible so this is a downfall for us as it's bright and keeps our kids attention rather than letting him drift to dreamland.
-
the power save mode for the LCD screen (to turn off after 2 mins) also turns off the audio, I HATE this!

So it forces you to use the VOX function (which has its limitations too, see below)
-
VOX has a lag (as does any audio on this camera - aprox 3-5 secs).
Sensitivity for us had to be set on high in order to work and even then it was pretty poor - it only picks up very loud sounds.
You dont need 2 sets of button groups doing the same thing and loose a vital function, dumb).

So in other words you can't really leave it on zoom which is impractical especially with a newborn.
-
This is a major problem for us and along with all the other issues , we stopped using the 2nd camera and went back to using an old monitor for one of the kids.
- cannot see or hear the monitor when using the menu.
Not practical or smart.

Luckily most (but not all) major things needed are on the regular buttons..
-
it takes alot of noise/LOUD noises to register on the sound bar.
My son will be sitting up asking me a question and you can clearly hear him but there is no noise registering on the sound bar....
