I'm completely disappointed and shocked that Britax is supposed to be the leader in car seats.

/>When we installed it we didn't notice but have been advised of it now after my son's been using it in grandma's car a few times (bought it a month ago for my son's stay with the grandparents while we are in the hospital with the new baby)
so it didn't get used/noticed until recently.
I'm pissed that we threw the box away and can't return this POS.

After looking for months, through tons of crib bedding for girls we settled on this one because it was super cute in the simple and classic way we wanted.
(We did not want the frilly, gaudy nonsense we kept seeing - or the typical elephants/animals).
But upon opening it today to get ready for baby (due in 3 weeks)

I was so disappointed by the quality.

The comforter is very very thin, hardly any batting inside and the material on the outside is very rough and thin too.
It would not provide very much warmth in the later years when it would actually be used, and I am doubtfully on how well it will stand up to washing.

It's so thin I would think the fabric might easily rip or degrade to holes over time, and I don't know if washing would soften them up much (or that I even want to attempt).
The sheets are paper thin, literally see through, and very rough.

I can't seeing them last either, especially being washed a million more times than the quilt.
The set we bought for our son through Babies R
Us years ago (which was primarily polyester to boot)

was a million times better than this.

We
love the design but the quality is so lacking we decided not to wash them yet and may return instead.
If we decide to keep them I'll update this in the future about if they softened up after washing and how they held up over time.
I like how the pockets tilt out so you can easily get stuff in and out (some styles have the pockets so close together you can't get stuff in and out of the pockets).
A little to stiff for my needs and preference even with the side and bottom removable inserts (in like the ones that are fully flexible so you can fit all shapes of things)
but I couldn't find those anywhere so this was the next best option.
Super soft and comfortable, has lasted a year now and is still holding up
Decent for the price.
It slides and shifts a bit
so I would hold or closely watch your child while using it, but for us it wasn't an issue because this was purchased for travel/use outside the home
so someone is always with the child.

For being able to take it anywhere (fold it up and put in a diaper bag etc), and that it's washable (even wiping or spraying it with sanitizer before putting it in the bag) is a huge plus and well worth the $10/12 price in my opinion.
Made potty training outside the home a lot easier.
Was a bit shocked fathead made this, the picture quality is quite poor, very grainy.
But from a distance, and higher up on the wall where we have it, it's not quiet as noticeable...
And my son loves monster trucks and said he didn't care, and this worked on our slightly textured walls (knockdown texture), so we kept it.

Sorry in advance for long review but I think its worth the time to read as I cannot understand how this is getting 10K 4&5 star reviews, this unit is poor quality and poor design, only good thing is the battery life.
The picture quality is horrendous; grainy and VERY blurry and it looks like the dying Summer Infant one I am trying to replace, yet this is brand new out of the box quality.
Screen is already 'pulsing' which is what our current Summer Infant one started doing when it started dying so I doubt this would last long...<br
/>(And I'll note here that Amazon sent a 2nd set because I was missing a piece of the first unit, and both have all the same poor picture and quality issues.
Could I have received 2 duds?

Possible, but not very likely...)

The IR sensitivity is poor, I can never get it out of night vision during the daytime unless the blinds are wide open and the ceiling light is on.
You have to go thru the menu button to get to these functions.
Yes there is a shortcut menu for the volume and brightness making it slightly easier, but zoom is still not readily available and I use that alot more than brightness
so that's a major pain for us.

These things may not annoy some people but for those of you who are used to smart technology, smart design/user friendliness and quick operation you will be disappointed and annoyed, especially at night if your having to fully get up and waste precious sleep navigating the menu to get to what you want.
Light up buttons when touched would have been a big help
but naturally they don't have that.
The tilt on the camera (up and down) is actually minimal compared to other brands.
Up high on the wall or shelf where we normally have our camera installed, it doesn't tilt down far enough to even see their crib/bed (it doesn't even hit bottom of the window on the opposite wall!).
It forces you to put the camera lower which will result in not seeing your child from above like most parents want (can't see if eyes are open or breathing etc).
Or it forces you to wall mount, which is what we now use even tho when you pan side to and side it skews the angles, but it's the only way to get a top ariel view of your child.
The speaker is on the back of the handheld unit.
You might think this is smart design but trust me it's anything but - it garbles and distorts the sound and you have to flip over the handheld unit to hear better.

The microphone is touch and go, sometimes it seems fine but often your child cannot understand you ( if he's of age to understand) in the talk back mode.

Overall
its a huge disappointment and downright poor quality and layout.

Why get a video monitor when you can get this thing!?
I love that it goes into sleep mode if baby is quietly sleeping.
If he starts crying or whining it turns on immediately and you could hear a pin drop with it!
It is very convenient and seems to have good range, as I can walk out to our garage with it on the other side of the house without any interference!
Our baby boy loves this thing.
Several nights when he was a newborn, the vibration was the only thing that would calm him down.
I still have it sitting in the bathroom to use for him

so I can get a shower every day, but the music stopped working after about 6 weeks (barely even used that option) and the vibrate doesn't seem as strong as it did when it was brand new...and yes, we have changed the batteries to see if that was the issue.
Overall, good bouncy seat...especially if you are a new mom and want to shower ;-)
Soft and high quality.
We have several of these and love how they glide over our sons baby skin.
They are gentle, yet get him clean!
We love these towels.
Soft on my sons skin, and large enough to swaddle him up after his bath...the best time to love on him!
We have several of these in different prints and would definitely recommend them!
Son loves these soothies.
We try to only give him the pacifier when he is so mad that we can't calm him down with walking/rocking/songs etc...
This thing was a lifesaver for my husband and I for the first month of my sons life.
He is a strong little thing and would wiggle out of swaddle blankets AND several brands of Velcro swaddles on the market.
This kept him wrapped up tight and sleeping for hours.
Now that he is almost 2 months, although he still fits in it, he does ok with the regular Velcro swaddles now...
Worked great for about 2 weeks after my son was born.
After he reached about 8.5 or 9 lbs it really wasn't supportive enough for him.
I would recommend this for while mom is in the hospital and shortly after birth.
I had a C-section and the midsection was very supportive for my surgical site and allowed me to hold my baby close without pushing on my incision.
Giving 3 stars due to the very short length of use I got out of this product and the high price paid.
I suppose I could still wear it under a cardigan or something for easy access breastfeeding on the go, but he wont fit in it anymore at all...
Very nice option to using disposable pads.
I love them for the spring/summer so that I can wear dresses without a bra underneath.

As for "blocking" the milk from coming out, I suppose it helped by compressing the nipple, but as soon as I removed one to breastfeed my son, the milk that had collected underneath the pad drained out and got all over my clothing.
Good thing I was at home.
I don't think this is something I would or could wear all day every day, but for the times I want to wear a dress, or sleep without a bra on, this is a great option.
As for the product, I am happy with it and would recommend...now that I know there is spillage involved with removal, I will tuck a cloth underneath prior to removing.
My husband loves this bag.
Easy for him to stay organized, and doesn't look like a girly mom's diaper bag that he has to carry.
It fits his tablet along with all the baby essentials.
Easy fabric to clean.
Would buy again, great deal.
Beautiful wearable fabric, easy to wipe off.
It's really the perfect size, fits all the necessities.
Anyone who says it is too small is definitely over packing (for one child)...this thing keeps me organized.
The zip down changing pad is great...pockets right above for the diaper cream etc.<br
/>We still have a larger messenger bag for longer day trips (like to the zoo etc) where we need to carry more than 3-5 diapers.
Good buy, would buy again.

They are annoying if you really have to pee...take a few seconds to open it, but they do the job.

Completely useless to me since I bought them specifically for this purpose.
This is a wonderful tool for steaming both the babies food and our veggies for dinner.
We have gotten a lot of use out of this.

construction_sents: You can gently tap the duck to switch between the three levels of brightness.
It's pretty much as I expected.
It has soft, natural bristles that are 7/8" deep and cover an oval about 3.5" long by 1.5" wide.
The body of the brush is wooden and smooth.
It appears well-made.
The package has 10 organic cotton wash cloths.
After washing warm/cold and and drying on low heat, these measure 9.75" x 9.75".
A fine terry cloth on one side and knit on the other.
Stitching is neat and even.
Machine wash cold, dry low, no bleach, iron on medium heat.
These come tightly packed in a zippered storage bag.
A little difficult to get out, and I'll never get them back in, but the storage bag can be used for other things.
The kneeler is a nice, thick 1.75" of a firm but comfortable foam encased in a water-resistance fabric.
Unfolded, it measures 22" long x 11" wide (or 11" square when folded).
The 22" long elbow protector has foam along the top and mesh pockets on the sides.
The sides hang down about 5.5".
There are suction cups on the underside to hold it in place.
We currently have nothing in the mesh pouches on the outer side and toys and two nearly empty shampoo bottles on the inside, and it's holding in place fine.
You also get a "sponge" pad.
All parts appear well made and like they'll last well.
This water resistant, folding knee rest pad was thinner than I expected.
The foam is firm but does give under the weight of a person kneeling on it, so it does pad hard floors.
It will probably last longer than a soft foam.
Because it is thin, I use it folded over (held closed with a Velcro strip near the handles).
This doesn't leave very much space for kneeling, but it works fine for a slim or petite woman.
(UPDATE: after trying to make this work for several weeks, we decided that it doesn't really work for a petite woman either.

It's better than nothing, but I would have returned it as being too thin if I had bought it.)

The foam area measures 10.5" long x 12.5" wide x 1 5/8" thick when folded.
The whole thing (not counting the handles) measures 22.5" long x 13.5" wide x about 0.75" thick when unfolded.
There's an unpadded trench between the two pads when unfolded.
The fabric doesn't have any obvious slip resistant backing, though it isn't slippery, either.
The stitching is neat, and the product appears to be well made.
This large silicone mat is thicker than most mats used as placemats or for making pastry.
I got this as a craft/painting mat for my young nieces.
They love to do watercolor, markers, crayons, ink stamps, and such.
This covers a large space on the table and protects the wood from excess water, paint, etc.
It holds in place well, and it's easy to clean up, especially if you do so immediately after the painting session.
Once dry, you can roll or fold the mat up, and it doesn't take up a lot of storage space.
If you need a mat this large, then this is a good product.
These two blankets come nicely wrapped, suitable for gifting.
These gray blankets look very well-made and have neat stitching.
The blankets have many very tiny holes in them; small enough that little fingers won't get caught but big enough to allow some venting.
The blanket measures 34" x 38" prior to being washed.
I haven't washed it yet, so I do not know if it shrinks.
The blankets are 100% organic cotton.
The packaging bears the global organic textile standard seal.
These 3 cabinet locks look like the ones my brother uses, so I got them for a visit from his family.
You press in the sides of the end piece to move the end sliding piece in or out along locking track.
It was hard to press in and move, but I could do it.
Only, you're supposed to be able to remove the end piece all the way off so this can be used on D-shaped handles in addition to knobs.
None of us could get the end pieces off.
The inside, extended length of the product (as far as I could manage) is 7.75" x 1.25" wide.
This infant bather looks nice, but it didn't work at all.
I got it for my 4 months old niece while that family was visiting us.
The bather snaps together.
It seems like only one way for it to go together, but I keep wondering if I somehow assembled it wrong because the cloth part is strung so tight that it's like a trampoline.
The baby just kept sliding to one side.
The sides are NOT large and actually aren't any higher than the center of the seat, so the baby wasn't held on the seat in any way.
No straps, no sides, and the whole thing wobbled as my sister-in-law tried to wash the baby with one hand and hold her in place with the other.
I followed the directions exactly.
When I moved the side clips higher up on the frame, the seat was a little deeper, but not enough to keep the baby upright and on the bather.
(She's not a highly wiggly baby, either.)
I'm disappointed that the bather didn't have the deep seat and high sides that are shown in the product pictures.
This large, metal "carry hook" measures 4" wide at it's widest by 6.25" tall.
The metal "rod" is about 3/8" thick.
The inside width of the smaller curved area is about 1.5" and on the wider curve is about 3".
The padding on one side is about 0.75" thick and nearly 4" long (exactly 3 7/8" long).
I like the padding that makes it easier on my hand to carry things on this hook.
The swinging opening part of the hook is easy to open widely to get straps through and onto the hook.
It holds the bags on the hook securely.
It's easier to carry several bags this way, either by hand or by hanging it on the stroller, walker, wheelchair, etc.
I'm very happy with this so far!
This cute Stroller Sloth has a soft fabric body.
Hanging from the sloth are a leaf that makes a crinkle sound when touched, a sun with a mirror in the center, and one of the sloths' arms with a handle for the baby to grip and pull.
As the arm is pulled down, the other arm extends...which, when the handle is released, vibrates the sloth as the top arm pulls him back close to the plastic branch that he's hanging from.

My 3-year-old niece also loves this toy, and we had to make it clear that it ultimately belonged to the baby.

Since we're still in winter and have been having a series of ice storms, we haven't been able to hang and try this swing out yet.

wash the brush before each use.

We got an Evenflo Infant to Booster Seat a couple of years back for when my niece visits, and we've been pleased with it.
So far, we like this one a little better as it's not quite as bulky (though it still looks plenty safe) and it's a little easier to install.
I'll admit it's also easier to install because we now have some experience with car seats so the sometimes-not-perfectly-clear-to-a-newbie instructions didn't make us pause this time.

Anyway, the straps come set for installing the seat in a rear-facing position.

For very young babies, there's extra padding you thread onto the front buckle straps to help hold them in place comfortably.
For front-facing toddlers, you can raise the back to extend the headrest upward.
I can't comment on daily use, but this works well for the occasional visits.

(We got this for the new addition that will soon be born.)

From

the box:
Rear facing for 4-50 lbs and 17-48 inches.
Forward facing for 22-65 lbs and 28-49 inches (for children at least 2 years old).

The Pooh 3-in-1 Convertible Crib is easy to assemble.
Using only the instructions that came with the crib, we were able to put the crib together in about 15 minutes.
The wood crib is sturdy and has the cute Pooh Bear design on the end.
It measures 53.75" across x 30.25" deep x 38.5" high.
The mattress can be adjusted between 3 heights as the baby starts to stand up.
It's nice that it is convertible into a toddler bed (with the Guardrail Kit, not included) so that we will be able to use it for several years.
We are currently using it for a two month old baby.
Happily, we happened to have a crib mattress as this does not come with one.
A standard size crib mattress fits.
This nightlight is made to look like a chick emerging from a broken egg.
The chick's head is made out of silicone.
A short press down on the head turns the light on or off.
When the light is on, press down on the head and hold as the brightness adjusts by dimming and then cycling back up to the brightest level.
Release when you reach your desired brightness level.
Once the brightness level is selected, it will remain at that level when you turn the light off and then on again.
The brightest light level provides enough light that you could read next to the light while the dimmest level provides just enough light that you can navigate a room without stumbling.

The LED light is a 3000k Warm White, so you don't need to worry about blue light.

The base is made out of a hard plastic and has a rounded rather than flat bottom.
The spot to plug the charging cable for the battery is in the back, and a USB charging cable is included.
They do not include a wall adapter, though.
The battery is 1200mAH and 3.7V. Charging can take up to 4.5 hours.
During charging, there is a red light next to the charging plug that turns on and blinks.
The light disappears when the battery is full.
On a full battery, the light can go continuously for eight hours at its brightest or 200 hours at its dimmest light level.
The nightlight also came with instructions, though they weren't always clear.
like the warm glow of the light, and it is easy to turn on and off as well as adjust the brightness.
While having a round base hasn't been a problem, it still startles me when it rocks when I bump it.
It's a cute idea for nightlight, and it's useful for when you need to check the baby or change a diaper at night.
In the pictures, I placed a letter next to the nightlight to show how well it illuminates by how easily you can read the letter.
I show the brightest level, a medium level, and the dimmest level.

construction_sents: Preferably a travel bag with a zipper and a handle.
I actually bought this from Target, but they're great.
I like that they're easy to take apart to wash.
Both my 3-year-old and 1-year-old use them.
They do not leak.
I frequently throw them into my purse for the kids when we're on the go; I wouldn't do this if they leaked.
And when my 3-year-old bit through the silicone straw (he has a tendency of biting through things), I called Tommee Tippee if find out how I could purchase more straws.
But instead of selling me more straws, they mailed me several straws free of charge.
They didn't even charge me for shipping.
I'm very impressed with this company.
There was nothing wrong with the straws; it was entirely my kid's fault for biting through the straws, but Tommee Tippee stands behind their products and wants their customers to be happy.
This is so rare these days.
I feel like every other company would have tried to charge me way too much for extra straws or quote me some ridiculous "shipping charge." Thank you, Tommee Tippee!
I would definitely buy and recommend your products because of your excellent customer service.
I've now owned this for 3.5 years and using it on my second child now.
/>The seat insert makes it easier to seat a baby that is just starting to sit, but isn't quite independent yet.
This was especially useful with my first child who has low muscle tone so needed support for a longer period of time.
This is the main reason I decided to buy and keep this tub.

The insert is also useful for before the sitting stage because it holds the baby's bum well from sliding down.

The sling was not very useful for us because our babies well all born rather big.

I think the sling is good for smaller newborns.

The squeeze bottle and fish toy were useless.
We never bothered with them.
I don't like: the spongy padding for the newborn's head gets dirty easily, but doesn't clean easily.

The little holes tend to gather residue.
If I try to scrub it, I end up tearing the spongy material because it's too cheap to be scrubbed.

I wish it was a removal flat pillow that could be machine washed.

Overall, a very good tub, but there are definite downfalls, especially in trying to keep it clean.
I like that the cup is clear so I can see how much my son has drank.
But the straw that came with it was bent so it was over half an inch off the bottom of the cup, so that he can't drink to the bottom.
That's a poor design.
But since I like that the cup is clear, I kept it and bought my own straws.
However, I would have preferred the clear straw that came with the cup if it wasn't so bent.
the company: PLEASE stop packing the straw bent.
I cannot straighten the original straw, so I end up needing to buy your super expensive replacement straws in order to get a straight straw.
I need my kid to drink all his milk.
A bent straw doesn't allow him to get to the bottom of the cup.
Milk got into the spinning mechanism, rendering the spinning part useless.
Maybe I got a faulty one.
/>Also, it can spin with sucking or blowing, so it seems to not be a good thing if you kid likes to blow.
Other than that, the cup works fine.
I like that the lower part of the straw is hard and can reach the bottom of the cup.
First off, it does work for calming the baby.
However, because it shuts off by itself after 15/30 minutes, the baby wakes up.
I found a portable sound machine to be much more effective, cheaper, better quality and easier to use.
These are pricey for what they are, but they're good.
We use two of them side-by-side on one side of a twin bed.
My son moves a lot in the bed so, it's necessary to have it all along the edge.<br
we did need to buy a thin box spring for the bed, though, because the frame with slats didn't work for putting on two of these.
They're fine if we only needed one, though.
I only wish they were softer.
Otherwise, these are exactly as advertised.

product itself is soft and cute.

I like that the floppy ears of the dog are perfect for the baby to put in his mouth.

I think this brush is even better than the use-at-home one that we have.
Drying rack could use improvements, but it's still very good.
My son tipped over on the floor with it.
We received this as a gift for my son (16 months) with Down syndrome.

He likes to play with it a lot, but I don't think I would ever purchase it myself due to these reasons:
1.
The purple phone isn't attached, so it keeps getting lost somewhere.

This seems like a silly oversight on the designers' part.
2.
The two different settings (defined by a book symbol and a musical note symbol) are not distinctly different enough.

I think the two settings should have completely different music and sounds, but a lot of the music and sounds are redundant.
3.
Due to the Down syndrome, my son has very little muscle tone.
At 16 months and 22 pounds, he still cannot stand on his own.
When I try to help him stand using this walker, he put his complete weigh on it, and it tips over.

This will probably not be an issue for typical children who can hold up some of their own body weight, but it doesn't work for us.

For
our purposes, I would give this 2 stars, but because I know my kid's issues are different from typical children, I upped it to 3 stars.
My son still plays with it a lot, but not for its intended purpose of being a walker.
We followed the advice of Kenneth M. Saltzman to double-baffle the cup for a slower flow, but it was still too fast.
Besides, we had a difficult time getting both baffles to click on properly.
Ultimately, we ended up getting a [[ASIN:B00FVZ92SU Reflo Smart Cup, a Smart Alternative to "Sippy Cups" (Clear - 2 Pack)]] instead, which has a much slower flow.
/>But to be fair, our baby (6-months-old) has an oral aversion, so he doesn't drink or eat like typical babies.
We are trying to use a cup for him upon the suggestion of his occupational therapist.
Because of health issues, he didn't have the energy to suck and and swallow his milk from a bottle.

And when his health issues were resolved, we realized that he actually lost the ability and desire to use the bottle altogether, which is why we're where we are... trying to get him to drink from a cup.
/>So, anyway, my review about the flow being too much may not be fair because of our baby's special circumstance.
Be sure to take this into account when making your purchasing choice.
We are still going to keep our cups in hopes of being able to use them when Baby gets older and hopefully masters the Reflo Cup.
For some reason, the "grass" I got is yellowish green.
I don't know why.
Everyone else I know who has one has really, really green grass.
/>But that really doesn't matter.
It still works the same way.
It's a good way to hold baby bottles, bottle caps, nipples, sippy cups, pump parts, etc.
We usually use ours after items have been washed, but before they get sanitized.
The grass and the tray underneath don't get dirty much because we only put clean items on it, but it's also very easy to clean.

Just a quick soap and rinse.

We can get 12-14 bottles and lids on it.
I'm sure it can fit more, but we're not very deliberate about lining up everything to conserve space.

After all, we sanitize at least once per day.

I'm
sure it's just as easy to use a regular dishrack based on how we use this, but the "grass" keeps us from mixing our things with Baby's things.
/>Hope your grass is greener...

We got this floor gym because (1) our baby's occupational therapist advised that we get one because he has low muscle tone and needs to work on reaching his arms, (2) it got good reviews here on Amazon.
I'm really not sure how this product got such high reviews.
It looks really poorly made and the design is just plain stupid.
When following the instructions for assembly, it definitely can cause the mat to close up on the baby.
To avoid this accidental trap, you actually need to NOT follow the assembly instructions and criss-cross the bars (like someone else had advised in the reviews).
/>But my chief complaint is how low the toys hang.
Two of the toys, in particular, actually get so close to my baby's face that they touch his face and makes him cross-eyed.
Instead of trying to reach for them, he just rolls aways from them.
One of the toys even touches his face!
The toys are supposed to be adjustable in length with the given rings, but each ring is at least 2-inches in diameter, so you can only adjust them 2-inches down if you want.

You can't actually hang them from the bar without the rings, so each toy is intrinsically going to be at least 2 inches down from the bar, which is how far they are when they stupidly hang so low that they hit my baby's face.

I grant that my child has a big head, but definitely not big enough to be his fault for such low-hanging toys.

And
this light-up tiger that everyone raves about in their reviews is just not interesting to our baby.

He doesn't even care.

To sum it up...

Pros:
/>Lots of black-and-white features<

br />Giraffe pillow is good for tummy time and encourages reaching in a tummy position

Cons:

/>Overly low-hanging toys (don't be fooled by the picture on the box or on the website)
Little flexibilty in getting toys to hang at the "perfect" length
Cheap-looking materials
Can be a trap when assembled according to manufacturer's instructions
I'll be looking for another floor gym.
I wanted to like this because I'm all about my baby having a clean nose, but the rounded tips make it hard to see what I'm getting at in his nose.
The rounded tips are a safety feature; I understand, but I just can't seem to work around them.
Maybe I'm doing something wrong.
Or maybe my baby's nostrils are too small; he's currently 6-months-old, but I've been trying to use this since he was a newborn.
Anyway, it still sits in his little hygiene bag, but I don't use it at all.
Instead, I either just use my pinky or the [[ASIN:B004JA1XB2 Baby Vac Nasal Aspirator 2012 Model]] aspirator (with saline) to get those boogers out.
Since my husband is the primary user of this product, I asked him for input when rating this product.
His quick response was, "I like it.
It's easy to use," thus the not-so-clever headline for this review.

/>In our household, this sterilizer is used multiple times a day... for two reasons: (1) I am an over-producer when it comes to breast milk, and (2) we're cheap and don't want to buy a whole much of bottles.
Currently, we mostly use the 5oz Medela bottles and 4oz cheap-o bottles that we got from the NICU.
/>We don't exactly follow the grooves in the sterilizer and have found our own way of arranging the bottles and lids.
We are able to sterilize 8 bottles and 8 lids at one time.
We also sterilize my pump parts in here a couple times per week.
We used to sterilize bottle nipples, but have not in a long time because our 6-month-old baby has a lot of health issues and actually lost the skill and desire to eat orally.
We feed him everything through an NG tube right now.
(It's hard, but that's the only way we can get him fed these days.
Sniff, sniff.)

It takes 3 minutes in the microwave, so it's pretty darn quick.

Our
only minor complaint about this sterilizer is that two of the grooves can sometimes cause the Medela bottles to topple.
But we realize that this is probably because this sterilizer was made for Philips AVENT bottles, so we don't feel right deducting any stars for this complaint.
I wanted to love this.
When the first one leaked, I assumed I must have had a faulty product since others who reviewed this loved it so much.
So, I exchanged it for another one.
The replacement leaked too.
Perhaps it was because I didn't store it upright.
I put it into a gallon-size Ziplock bag and threw the whole thing into my diaper bag.
It was sideways, upside-down, maybe sometimes even upright...
I don't know.
But each time, there was a little leakage into the Ziplock bag.
Not a lot leaked out (just a little), but I guess I was hoping for zero leakage.
(Were my hopes too lofty?)

Thankfully, I had the plastic bag; otherwise, items in the diaper bag would have gotten wet too.

Otherwise, I think this is a great concept.
It's a simple, practical and convenient design.

Maybe it's the quality that is just lacking.

I wouldn't automatically discourage others from getting it, especially if you don't just throw it (any which way) into your diaper bag like I did.
If you have an upright pocket on your bag or if you have a way to keep it upright, it's perfect for you!
It doesn't get anything out.
It's completely useless to us.
We prefer the Nose Frida for when outside of the house and the Baby Vac for when at home.
This is too big for my baby's mouth and there don't seem to be enough holes on it.
The [[ASIN:B005KWLEVW
[Award Winning] Kidsme Food Feeder (Large size)]] is much better.
/>However, it is easy to clean and has an attractive look to it.
It's really hard to put on, and even harder when Baby is already sitting on the Megaseat.
This is a very poor design.
You'd think they could do better.
Since our baby has Down syndrome and other health issues, we had him lying down all the time.
Because of this, he started developing a major flat head.
The instructions say to not use it for sleep, but we did because he couldn't turn due to low muscle tone.
After only a few weeks of using this, I started noticing the difference.
The proof was when we went to see his physical therapist for his first visit and she commented that I must carry him a lot because his head is nice and round!
Yay for round heads!
heldout_sents: it has no function and just causes leakage.
A pocket in the back is already sufficient.
I only like it for its size.
In summary, it's expensive, the fleece clings on to poop and the hole in the front allows for leakage.
I hate that I didn't have another choice in getting an XL pocket diaper (or actually a tunnel diaper since there are holes in the back and in the front).

Positives:
Good quality
High weight capacity
Comfortable<

Areas of improvement:
No pocket to keep the metal pieces when the chair is not in use
No travel bag
*These are very important when dealing with baby gear.
Parts need to be kept together so you don't inadvertently lose anything, and a travel bag is important so you can easily lug it around.

construction_sents: It also plays music, if your child needs that.
Munchkin products have always impressed us with their smart features and functionality, and this noise machine is no different.
I really liked these cups for about two days!
They're cute, the handles are good for little hands, and they don't spill.
Unfortunately, they're really easy to open, so once my toddler figured it out (which didn't take long)
These are super easy to install and work perfectly.
We pair this with a Munchkin stepstool, and my toddler is able to easily reach the faucet to wash his hands.
Munchkin has the most ingenious baby/toddler products, and this is no exception.
These plastic feeding spoons are perfect to throw in the diaper bag.
I love that they come with a case because it keeps the spoon clean for when you need it!
The shape is also great, I love that the spoon is deep so it actually holds purees pretty easily.
That makes it a great spoon to feed with, but also for your little one to learn on.
I try to use micellar water, rather than wipes, on my baby's face because wipes can be so drying.
But when I got these, I decided to try them out at the dinner table, to wipe off his hands and face after eating.
I was concerned that, like regular wipes, they'd be too drying.
But I'm so pleased that they aren't at all -- the moisturizer they contain are perfect.
They don't dry delicate skin out, but they are strong, thick wipes that stand up to big messes.
I'll definitely be buying more of these.
These bowls work really well for our toddler who has learned not to throw plates and bowls, but he does like to pick them up and turn them upside down.
They won't lift up unless you pick specifically at the base, which makes them great to teach kids how to use bowls.
They rinse easily and go through the dishwasher well.
While I hate single-use plastics, I admit I absolutely love these placemats.
They're perfect for when you're out and about with your infant or young toddler and they aren't quite ready to use plates yet.
My infant tends to chew on the side of the table (yes, he's at that age) when he's in a high chair, and this at least means he's not chewing the table!
It sticks well, the adhesive pull off strips are a little annoying, but once it's on it stays in place.
I always have one of these tucked into my diaper bag, and they've served me well.
We are slowly trying to teach our one-year-old to hold his own spoon and these are just the ticket.
We switch between these and the softer, silicone spoons (also by Munchkin, I love their dishes for kids) and he's learning to use a metal spoon well.
The handle is chubby enough for him to grip easily, and when he's finally ready to feed himself, I think these will do nicely.
For now, he sometimes gets food into his mouth but mostly just bangs them around.
It's nice that they're well made and stand up well to this kind of abuse, so I know they'll last a long time.
We only used pacifiers during naptime for our little one, but this was a great little soothie.
It's nice that the attached stuffed animal kept it in place while the baby was sleeping.
It meant we couldn't put it in the crib at night, but that's ok --
it's easy enough to detach!
And when they get dirty, you can just throw them in the washing machine.
This is a perfect gift set for your own child or someone with a baby on the way.
It has everything you need for feeding time!

We love the compartment plate for more complex meals, but the larger plate without compartments is great for when babies are learning to pick up food (but also to help teach kids not to throw their plates!)
The bowl is perfect for smaller meals or snacks, and the cup is great for pre-sippy cup days.
All in all, this is a great set.
I started using these spoons when we first introduced solids to our baby, and we absolutely love them.
They're soft, so there's no concern with hurting the baby's soft palate, and the choke guard is such a nice feature.
They hold food well and are very easy to clean.
Now that we've moved onto more complex foods, the spoon is a little small, but they're great for him to hold when he's learning to feed himself
We've been using these sippy cups with our one year old as he's been transitioning from the bottle to a cup.
It's taken a little instruction, but in just a couple of weeks, he's a pro at holding the cup by himself and drinking out of it.
He never had a problem getting used to the mouthpiece, and it's really nice that even when he bangs it on on the ground (which happens all too often), there aren't any spills.
A bonus: You can snap off the handles and it fits nicely in the bottle compartments of a diaper bag!
We really love this shopping cart/high chair cover.
It comes with its own bag, so it's relatively easy to store, and it is machine washable (and durable enough to go through multiple washes).
It's perfect for when you don't feel like wiping down shopping carts and high chairs, and provides a soft surface for baby (the padded leg holes are especially nice).
It also has some attached toys.
It is quick to install (just elastic) and is a great idea for any parent!
Aquaphor has been a staple in our house ever since having a baby.
It cures all ills, providing a protective barrier for diaper rash, drool rash, and other skin ailments, including small cuts.
It also works as a serious moisturizer, which is important if you live in a dry area or have a winter baby.
This set includes one large tub, which will last months, and a smaller tube that I throw in the diaper bag.
I can't say enough good things about Aquaphor and how much we use it.
I absolutely love these sleep sacks.
They're soft and thick, perfect for a cooler night or a summer one with the a/c blasting.
I love the feel of them and baby seems so cozy when wearing them.
My baby is 9 months old and in the 80th percentile for height, and he still fits in a 3 to 6 month size (though it's getting snug).
It's nice that these have some longevity because they are expensive.
The only complaint I have is the reverse zipper -- we don't need to do diaper changes at night, but it is often a wrestling match to get baby into the sleep sack at night.
I'd prefer a regular zipper you don't have to hook, or a double zipper.
I love that these pacifiers are silicone and that they are one piece.
It makes them very easy to keep clean (just throw them in the dishwasher!) and ensures water or liquid doesn't get stuck anywhere.
It also doesn't have any annoying crevices.
The only reason I knocked off one star is for some reason, my baby doesn't love these.

He'll tolerate them if they're the only pacifiers we offer, but he doesn't love them the same way he loves his others (I don't think this is the fault of the pacifier, just that every baby is different).
Pity because the colors and feel of these are really really nice!
The Tommee Tippee portable blackout shade does exactly what it proposes and does it well.
You unfold the curtain, adjust it to width with the velcro strips and then suction it to the window.
It holds fast and blocks out virtually all of the light that would otherwise be keeping your little one awake.

There's only a slight bit of light leak around the window edges, but not enough to impact sleep.

This shade was a lifesaver during our summer vacation when the sun was rising very early and our kid's pack-and-play was in an office space without good curtains.
/>The shade also works really well as a drape over a pack and play.
You can turn it into a bit of a tent that cuts out some of the light and noise that might keep a kid from napping.
These size 3 diapers are comparable to the Honest brand.
I usually use Honest but have started buying Pampers Pure in this 60 count box size to send to day care.
His carers really like this brand as he hasn't had a single leak or blow out with these Pampers.
My baby has very sensitive skin, but these diapers work really well for him.
They are very soft and unscented.
All in all, these are a win.
The Apple Oatmeal Raisin with Cinnamon flavor of Sprout's organic pouches has been a real hit with my nine month old.
He's been having this flavor for breakfast and he absolutely loves it.
We go through pouches quickly in our house, so ordering through Amazon is an economical way to handle the pouch situation.
It's great having a travel crib that doubles as a play yard!

The dual purpose fixture is, in particular, really great for travelling.

Day-to-day we keep the play yard set up in our living space to help corral the little one when we have to step away.
He doesn't mind spending a bit of time inside and seems to enjoy playing against the mesh walls.
We have also used the nice, thick, playyard pad outdoors on rough ground to give the baby a safe place to crawl and play.
/>As a travel crib the Skip Hop also works very well.
If you're not bringing the larger pad, then it packs down to a nice compact package that isn't too heavy.
It sets up and breaks down quickly and easily.

And it's perfectly easy to convert back and forth between playyard and crib modes.

The fabric feels nice and is holding up well to typical baby messes.
We usually use Honest diapers so I was eager to try these Pampers Pure diapers out to compare.
They are very soft but hold waste very well.
We don't ever really have a leaks problem and they stay snug, even on a very active child.
My only issue is the tabs -- the material holding them on is very thin and delicate.
It's fine once they are on the child, but I have ripped many a diaper trying to get them on!
I wish they would reinforce that area, but other than that, these are great diapers.
This fork and spoon set is really great for clumsy toddler hands as they are learning to eat with real silverware.
The handles make them easy to grip, and the blue color is cute (and also unisex, honestly, with the shade of blue it is).
These also hold up well in the dishwasher.
They're a good price and durable, can't ask for much more than that with baby products!
These child locks do a great job keeping kids out of kitchen cabinets.

The magnetic locks are very easy to install and use and offer great protection.

I particularly like that you can leave the magnetic “key” in place if you’re going to be opening a particular drawer lots of time and don’t want to keep fiddling with the lock.
And the key can be hidden up on a high counter, keeping clever kids from figuring out how to open the lock by themselves.
The ITOOL child locks do the job.
And the 10 pack is perfect for your whole kitchen.
/>The locks are super easy to install and their double sided tape offers plenty of adhesion to keep a toddler from yanking open a cabinet.

The magnetic style locks look nice, operate easily, can be left in place if you’re opening a particular cabinet multiple times, and can be easily hidden away from clever kids who might figure out how to open the tab-style locks.
The Toolic magnetic child locks are super easy to install.
The double sided tape that holds them to the cabinet doors provides plenty of adhesion to keep even a strong (and strong-willed) two year old out of the cleaning products.
Like most OXO products, these little utensils are functional, sturdy, ergonomic, and nice looking.
Our little one finds it easy to eat out of them and we find them easy to use to feed him.
/>In particular, it's nice that these have long handles.
Too many kid spoons are short and stubby and leave your hand exposed to all of their messy eating.
The included carrying case allows us to carry these around in a diaper bag while keeping them clean and organized.
Our kid absolutely loves playing with his trains and cars on the green top of this play table.
It's at a perfect height and has a nice sturdy surface.

It's got nice rounded corners that are kid-safe and it's lightweight enough to shuffle around the room when we need to make additional space.

The table was very easy to assemble and is sturdily made.
The lift-up table top also offers excellent storage underneath the table for toys.
The only down side is that the built-in drawers are a bit shallow.
They work well for Thomas toy trains but are too small for larger toy cars.
I was really excited to use this playmat outside on our porch.
I’m not comfortable putting our baby on the furniture because he’ll roll off, but the ground is just too hard.
Unfortunately, this doesn’t work as well as I’d hoped.
While the thinness means it folds up incredibly well, fitting into a small pouch, it also means that there is absolutely no padding.
This would work well in the grass, but not on any sort of even slightly hard surface.
The weights work reasonably well, but the mat will blow away on a windy day.
While it doesn’t work as well as I’d hoped, it lives in the car and we still find it very useful for picnics and other events.
My six-month-old loves this dinosaur teether.
He chomps on it constantly and his pudgy hands don't have a problem keeping a grip on it.
I like that there are multiple shapes on it
so he gets different sensations on his gums.
He isn't teething yet, but I love that when he is, I can just stick this in the freezer and then give it to him.
I also love how easy it is to clean -- wipe it down or stick it in the dishwasher and it's as good as new.
Our 6 month old isn't quite ready to sit up on his own, but he's far beyond the stage where's he's content to lay on his back and miss out on the world around him.

He want's to see what's going on!

Enter
the Fisher Price Sit-Me-Up.
Our little guy absolutely loves this seat.
He can see what's going on.
He has plenty of support, so he can hang out in it unassisted for quite a long time.
And it has enough of a ledge to let him keep a selection of toys in front of him.
the parents, the seat was a breeze to assemble, it is easy to transport around the house, and it is very easy to fold flat and store.
It may be an item that will have a limited useful life for you and baby, but it sure is a big value add while you need it.
The Maxi Cosi Magellan is made from premium materials and with a good eye toward design.
It fits in very well in our luxury car.
I particularly like the soft, stretchy material.
It feels nice to the touch and is good at disguising baby messes.

If you have a nice car and want a seat the blends in to your black interior, I think that you would be hard pressed to do better than the Magellan.

We currently have the Magellan in rear facing mode.
It was easy to install, though it took a minute of examining the routing of the straps on the seat and in the manual to understand how to access and route everything.
Once I verified that it was properly installed the seat feels rock-solid.
With the SIPS protection and multi-point restraint, I feel comfortable knowing that my kid is cocooned in all of the latest safety features.
/>Other excellent features include the cup holders, which function perfectly and remove easily for cleaning.
I also appreciate how easy it is to adjust the seat and how flexible it will be as my kid grows.
/>My only (very modest) gripe is that the supplemental support pillows for small infants can tend to wander since they are not affixed.
This JJ Cole diaper bag backpack is durable and holds everything I need for a six month old.
I keep diapers, wipes, an outfit change, a changing pad, a blanket, pacifiers, toys, and more in this diaper bag, and I still have room to tuck my wallet, keys, and phone in it.
The padded shoulder straps make it comfortable to wear, and the backpack style is incredibly convenient because my hands are free.
The stroller clips work well — just make sure that you don’t have it weighed down too heavy or the stroller will tip.
I knocked off one star because while the wipeable material is practical and works well, the rose gold accents and large zippers look a little cheap, especially given the price of this bag.
These choices were likely made to increase longevity, which I understand, but it doesn’t look as good as it could.
While we’re still using it primarily for an infant in rear-facing mode, we’re already in love with this car seat.
It installs easily, the fabric feels high quality, and kiddo—whose opinion really matters here—seems to really like it.
It also just feels extremely sturdy and robust; I have a lot of confidence that it serves it’s intended purpose—keeping my kid safe.
/>And since we needed a second seat for the other car, it’s great that it will adapt as the little nugget grows.

Having two infant seats, two rear-facing seats, and then two booster seats was going to feel excessive.

The adjustments are super easy with the no retread harness and the big easy buck makes it easy to get kid in and out.
The recline is also great for keeping kiddo at a comfortable angle.
And it’s narrow enough that it doesn’t crowd out all of the space in our back seat.
We tried pretty much all of the baby tubs and this is the best, hands down.
Most importantly, the seat has the best bum support that we've seen, so our squirmy water-loving baby can't unseat himself and slip down so that his head goes under.
The drain plug is also cleverly designed.
We like to fill up the tub, wash the baby, drain it while he's inside and refill the tub quickly from the shower wand.
That way he gets a rinse in clean water rather than just sitting and playing in the filthy wash water.
The Munchkin tub feels like it's made from high quality materials and is proving to be sturdy so far.

We also like that the soft back support pad goes up so high and really supports baby's head.

We've tried the competitors and found them lacking.
The Puj tub was great for a few weeks of sink washing, but the baby outgrew it almost instantly.
The Boon tub has a weird removable bum support that let the baby squirm off and dunk himself into the bath.
And the weird mesh thing from Buy Buy Baby requires you to fill up the whole bath tub, which takes forever and is hard to get the temperature right.
This is a top-notch baby monitor that is the best quality money can buy.
The picture quality is especially great.
The standalone baby monitors really can’t compare; the only one that can is the Arlo Baby, which we also have.
Using these two side by side, I prefer the Arlo Baby because it comes with 7 days of free video.
The Nanit Plus comes with free history, but only for a year — then you have to subscribe.
Otherwise, this camera is great, though, especially if you don’t mind paying for the insights.
The night vision is especially good quality, and it’s nice that you can use it on up to 10 devices — we keep the app on a couple of iPads as well as our phones.
It’s a great baby monitor, especially because we haven’t had any connectivity issues.
Philips Avent bottles have kept our babies fed and happy.
The anti-colic inserts and air-free technology really do seem to make a difference.
We've had much fewer problems with gas and reflux than many of our friends and family.
We've got a pile of them in different sizes and I'd purchase them all again in an instant.
I really, really like this Philips audio baby monitor.
It's perfect for mobility around home and for travel.

We've been extremely pleased with the entire Philips Avent line and this product is no exception.

We

have one of the fancy Arlo video monitors set up over the crib, but it's basically impossible to move it around the house to follow your baby and it requires local wifi set up, so it's not good for traveling to hotels or family's houses.

This
Philips monitor is an excellent mobile solution for monitoring the kids.
It's easy to move around the house or set up on the go.
And you don't have to listen to every little noise in the room, since the monitoring LEDs show you when there's noise in the room.
heldout_sents: This is perfect because you can put the name label on the inside of the cup and insert it into the outer part.
We love all of Munchkin's products, they're so innovative, and this is no different.
My toddler still uses a pacifier at night, and he loves these.
The designs are cute and I appreciate how the design of them doesn't hold moisture around his mouth.
We'll definitely be buying more of these.
This is a nice, multipurpose sound machine for a baby, toddler, or kid’s room.
I don’t use the bulk of the features on it — just the white noise — because I have a young toddler who doesn’t sleep with any sort of light.
I’ve tested the projector feature, and it works nicely, as does the nightlight.

construction_sents: The design is colorful and cute, perfect for a 2--3 year old.
My only gripe is that even with a very small child it was snug around the thighs.
The waist was fine but the thigh holes were very small and snug.
I purchased these spoons as a complement to the forks from Gerber.
They are sturdy and well-made and perfect for small hands.
My almost 3 year old has no issues gripping or using these spoons.
I also appreciate that the spoon itself is a good size without being too large.
We have a lot of spoons that are super tiny and therefore almost useless in scooping up yogurt or applesauce.
These are just right in size for my preschooler.
We've been using Luvs for a while now since my son was an infant and I really like them.
They have always worked well to keep daytime leaks in and I love that they are so much cheaper then other brands but work just as well.

The only issue we have with them (and this has only been an issue since my son turned about a year and a half) is that now that my son is older and drinks more throughout the day, these do not work overnight to keep leaks in.
His bladder has gotten just too big I guess for the diaper to handle.

We use the [[ASIN:B005M6E1DY Huggies OverNites Diapers, Size 6, Big Pack, 44 Count]] at night to keep leaks in.

Other
then the night time issue, I have no product quality complaints.
I am however sad to see the price go up and the amount of diapers offered go down.
I cannot see any product changes in the new diapers which indicate the need for the price hike.
They work the same as before and other then a design change on the diaper, look the same.
I buy these refills for our [[ASIN:B00BLVQIMG
Diaper Genie Elite Diaper Disposal Pail with Refill, 270-Count]].
They fit in the pail well and do what they are designed to do.
My only suggestion for improvement would be to have the end of the bags be connected to the plastic ring somehow.
I dislike when I get towards the end of the pack and I throw a diaper in and the whole bag falls into the pail.
I feel so wasteful having to cut the life of a bag short because it won't stay in the ring.
Sometimes I'll cut off the filled portion and the remaining bag isn't quite long enough
and I end up pulling the whole rest of it out.
If it was glued in there somehow, then I could use up every last inch of the bags without wasting any.
I've seen people mention that I am going to reiterate is how to get more out of your bags.
When it's time to empty, I push down whatever diapers are in the pail and squeeze out the extra air.
I keep doing this until I have a compact air-free package of dirty diapers
and then I cut the whole load off and tie it up.
This will save you a lot of bag length.
Try it next time and check out the difference between where you would have had to cut before and where you ended up cutting after pushing the air out.
This technique will prolong the bags.
I purchased these to prevent a headstrong toddler from opening the door to the deck and downstairs.
They are fairly easy to open and re-close and are working well to prevent him from using the door knob.

I believe he is (and this could be because I am biased) a fairly intelligent guy and is very good with using tools and puzzles and yet he has not been able to work around these covers and get them off or use the door.
